## Static/global initialization lambda boundary and diagnostic ranges

- problem type: static/global definite-initialization must not treat nested lambda or anonymous-function bodies as immediately executed static initializer effects, while static/global field and constructor-completion diagnostics must use the repository's token/header range policy.
- root cause: the shared initialization-flow expression dispatcher entered `CfirAnonymousFunctionExpression` bodies, so assignments and reads inside lambda arguments affected the enclosing static initialization state. Immutable static `let` assignment classification also treated nested assignments in a constructor/static-init context too broadly. Separately, `TYPE_UNINITIALIZED_STATIC_FIELD` fixtures still expected whole declarations, and `CLASS_UNINITIALIZED_FIELD` on explicit constructors still included the body braces.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all tmp/codex-static-let-lambda-assign-probe.cj` produced no diagnostics for a static `let` initialized only inside a lambda argument; `tmp/codex-static-let-lambda-reassign-probe.cj` reported `sema_cannot_assign_to_immutable` on the nested `CTX = 10` assignment after a prior direct static-init assignment. Official implementation was traced through `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp` `IsUsedInInitFunction`, `NotAssignableVariable`, `CheckLetFlag`, `CheckLetFlagInMemberAccess`, and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Diags.cpp` `DiagCannotAssignToImmutable`, which uses the assignment expression as the main diagnostic range.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/cfa/FirPropertyInitializationAnalyzer.kt` and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/expression/FirReassignmentAndInvisibleSetterChecker.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt` and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirAssignmentLegalityChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: keep static/global initialization in the shared flow owner, but model anonymous functions as value creation rather than immediate execution, and classify immutable-field assignment through the same constructor/static-init ownership instead of fixture-local branches.

## While-let expression raw build, pattern scope, OR diagnostics, recovery, and Option target typing

- problem type: `while-let-expr` LLT failures across PSI and light-tree paths: PSI raw CFIR did not build `let` conditions, let-pattern bindings had incorrect loop-condition/body scope and redeclaration behavior, `||` conditions could introduce pattern variables without `VAR_IN_OR_CONDITION`, malformed `while (let ... <- ... {}` recovery treated the loop body as a trailing lambda, and `None` inside assignment/tuple/call contexts lost the expected `Option<T>` target type.
- root cause: PSI `CjIfExpression` and `CjWhileExpression` looked for `LET_EXPRESSION` as a direct child instead of inside the `CONDITION` container. Condition pattern bindings were registered for expression resolution but the conflict checker did not model a non-do-while loop condition and body as one local declaration scope, so body redeclarations were missed while outer declarations could be treated as conflicts. The expression checker set did not walk `CfirBinaryOpKind.OR` for visible let-pattern introductions. The parser did not mark malformed while-let condition boundaries strongly enough, allowing the following block to be consumed as a trailing lambda. Finally, tuple element checking and call-completion result writing did not reuse the existing no-arg enum constructor expected-type rule, so `None` stayed unresolved or candidate-diagnostic-backed when its expected type was `Option<T>`.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` on a minimized `while (false || let Some(b) <- a) { return b - 1 }` reports `sema_var_in_or_condition`; `external/cangjie_compiler/include/cangjie/Basic/DiagRefactor/DiagnosticSema.def` defines that diagnostic, and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/IfExpr.cpp` `CheckBinaryCondition` collects variables in `||` and diagnoses the first introduced variable. `cjc` on `while (let Some(b) <- a) { let b = b }` reports redefinition for the body declaration and unresolved use on the initializer side; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckPattern.cpp` explicitly documents that `while (let a <- 1) { let a = 1 }` conflicts with a definition in the while-let body. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Collector.cpp` documents the official `while (let p <- i) { t }` scope shape.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/raw-fir/psi2fir/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/builder/PsiRawFirBuilder.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/raw-fir/light-tree2fir/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/lightTree/converter/LightTreeRawFirExpressionBuilder.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/ArgumentUtils.kt`.

## If-let enhanced condition scope, OR diagnostics, or-pattern legality, and libast quote typing

- problem type: current `if_let_expr.enhancedcondition` LLT failures across PSI and light-tree paths plus macro libast failures under `macro.llt.if_let_expr.enhancedcondition`: let-pattern condition bindings did not consistently reach the right-hand side of `&&` and the successful then branch, `||` let-pattern diagnostics used incomplete condition-level range/source rules, let-condition or-pattern legality was only checked in match patterns, and `quote(...)` in libast array literals had no resolved token-stream type.
- root cause: enhanced-condition body resolve was not fully aligned to official `CheckCondition` / `CheckBinaryCondition` control flow, the local redeclaration checker did not model if-let condition bindings and then-branch top-level declarations as one fresh branch scope, the existing or-pattern checker was match-only and reported variable binding diagnostics inappropriate for condition-level `||`, and `CfirQuoteExpression` was not dispatched through expression resolve; when synthesized manually, it used the wrong libast result type for array-element inference.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/IfExpr.cpp` `CheckCondition` / `CheckBinaryCondition` resolves `&&` left-to-right, diagnoses variables introduced under `||`, and still checks both sides; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LoopExprs.cpp` routes while conditions through the same condition checker; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Collector.cpp` documents condition and successful-branch scope collection; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckPattern.cpp` contains the shared or-pattern binding/kind legality checks; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/QuoteExpr.cpp` uses the desugared quote expression type; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Desugar/DesugarMacro.cpp` desugars `quote(...)` to `std.ast.Tokens(...)`, and `analysis/stubs/testData/builtins/std.ast.cjo.decompiled.text.cj` confirms `class Tokens` and libast constructors consuming `std.ast.Tokens`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirAbstractBodyResolveTransformerDispatcher.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/expression/FirExpressionChecker.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirConflictsDeclarationChecker.kt`.

## Flow expression desugaring, function-value context, and constructor argument diagnostics

- problem type: flow expressions must resolve `|>` / `~>` through the shared call resolver, preserve function references as function values, recover from root operand errors without cascading unresolved calls, and zero-parameter constructor calls with supplied arguments must report shared argument-mapping diagnostics on the full call source.
- root cause: `transformFlowExpression` desugared pipeline uniformly as `right.invoke(left)`, so function references, callable values, overload filtering, and expected function-type resolution did not follow the official flow-call shape. Composition operands were not resolved in flow function-value context, and root operand errors could leave the composition initializer with a non-callable error type, causing `let h = f ~> g; h(-1)` to emit a secondary unresolved `h`. Constructor argument diagnostics also treated named arguments on zero-parameter constructors as missing names and used argument-only source ranges.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Desugar/DesugarInTypeCheck.cpp` `TryDesugarFunctionCallExpr`, `DesugarPipelineExpr`, and `DesugarCompositionExpr` show that pipeline builds `right(left)`, composition builds `composition(TryDesugar(left), TryDesugar(right))`, and non-function operands are converted to `expr.()` only when needed. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/BinaryExpr.cpp` `ChkFlowExpr` resolves operands under diagnostic suppression, calls normal call checking on the desugared expression, and recovers root operand errors without cascading outer diagnostics.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt` for context-dependent callable references and synthetic outer-call resolution, plus the existing CFIR call-resolution counterparts `CfirCallResolver`, `PostponedArgumentsAnalyzer`, and `functionTypeForFunctionValueCandidate`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/candidate/Candidate.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/tower/TowerLevelHandler.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirMapArguments.kt`, `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/collectors/components/ErrorNodeDiagnosticCollectorComponent.kt`.
- repair principle: express flow through the existing call/candidate/constraint framework and use `ConeErrorType.delegatedType` only as a recoverable callable type carrier, so unresolved operand roots remain the only diagnostics while later function-value calls still resolve through normal callable-value candidates.
- fixtures covered: `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.flow_expr.FlowExprGenerated` and `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.flow_expr.FlowExprGenerated`, including `testPipeline7`, `testComposition5`, `testComposition91`, `testErrPipeline00`, `testErroFlowLambda`, `testPipeline9`, and the exposed `testPipeline8` guard.

## Generic static member access through type-parameter upper bounds

- problem type: static member access through exposed generic type parameters must select the closest static implementation from class/interface upper-bound intersections, diagnose instance members on generic qualifiers as generic static-access errors, preserve private static access-control diagnostics, and report inherited upper-bound return-type conflicts separately from call-resolution ambiguity.
- root cause: type-parameter qualifier static scopes concatenated upper-bound static scopes without modeling the official closer-implementation merge, so inherited static functions from interface/class upper bounds could remain ambiguous. Generic qualifier instance-member access reused the ordinary type-name non-static diagnostic instead of the exposed-generic diagnostic. Declaration-side generic upper-bound checking did not run the official inherited-member conflict pass over `where T <: C1 & I`, so `INHERIT_MEMBER_TYPE_INCONSISTENT` was missing even when call resolution correctly chose the class implementation.

Official implementation was traced through `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp`, `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckReference.cpp`, `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/GenericInheritanceChecker.cpp`, `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/MergeInheritedMemberHelper.cpp`, and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/StructInheritanceChecker.cpp`.

## Generic enum constructor member access inference and variadic argument shape

- problem type: generic enum constructor member access must infer the enum owner type from member-call arguments when possible, keep ordinary `Array<T>` arguments out of the variadic element path, and still report a bare generic enum constructor when the owner type cannot be inferred.
- root cause: substituted enum member value parameters were copied from the symbol's cached resolved return type instead of the declaration parameter type, so `a16(x: Array<T>)` could degrade to an element-level expectation. The call argument checker also treated a single `Array<Int64>` argument mapped to a variadic-capable `Array<T>` parameter as a variadic element, fixing `T` to `Array<Int64>` and producing `Array<Array<Int64>>`. Finally, the bare-generic access checker handled class/typealias classifiers but not enum constructor symbols whose generic owner remained uninstantiated after call completion.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/type_infer/infer_member_access_with_enum_ctor_succ.cj` produced no errors; only the unused-variable warning for `v`. A marker-free probe for `infer_member_access_with_enum_ctor_fail.cj` produced `sema_unable_to_infer_generic_func` on `T1.a16` and `sema_generic_type_without_type_argument` on `T1`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/DeclAttributeChecker.cpp` `CheckEnumAttribute` enables `PUBLIC` on enum constructors; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp` treats enum constructors as global decls and builds owner mappings for enum-constructor member access; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeArgumentInference.cpp` / `TypeCheckUtil.cpp` contain the `IsEnumCtorWithoutTypeArgs` target-typing and inference rules.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/CheckArguments.kt`, `CreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`, `ResolutionStages.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/FirClassSubstitutionScope.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/scopes/impl/CfirClassSubstitutionScope.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCheckDispatchReceiver.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCheckArguments.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/CfirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/EnumConstructorTargetTyping.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirGenericBareClassifierAccessChecker.kt`.

## Lambda fold pipeline PSI type-argument ownership and function-value completion

- problem type: `LambdaGenerated.testTestFold` PSI path reported `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_NO_MATCH` / `NO_MATCHING_OPERATOR_INVOKE` on `fold { ... }(Nil)` while the light-tree path had already resolved the same fixture; the lambda receiver subtree also needed completed function-value types to prevent stale postponed-lambda diagnostics.
- root cause: PSI `CjCallExpression.typeArgumentList` recursively searched arbitrary callee syntax and could capture a type argument from a trailing lambda body, so the outer function-value `invoke` for `fold { ... }(Nil)` received a spurious explicit type argument. Completion writing for function-call receivers also had to write back the resolved receiver subtree for nested function-value invocations.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/lambda/test_fold.cj` exited `0` with no diagnostics. Official flow behavior for this fixture family follows the already traced `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Desugar/DesugarInTypeCheck.cpp` `TryDesugarFunctionCallExpr` / `DesugarPipelineExpr` rules: `a |> f` is checked as `f(a)` through normal call checking.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/psi/psi-api/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/psi/KtCallExpression.kt`, where `typeArgumentList` is the call's own `TYPE_ARGUMENT_LIST` child and `typeArguments` are not found by recursive search into lambda bodies.
- CFIR owner files changed: `psi/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/psi/CjCallExpression.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/CfirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`, and `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirMapTypeArguments.kt`.
- repair principle: keep type-argument ownership in the PSI call model and function-value receiver completion in the shared call completion writer, so synthetic `invoke` calls never inherit type arguments from receiver expressions or lambda bodies.
- fixtures covered: `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.lambda.LambdaGenerated.testTestFold`, `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.lambda.LambdaGenerated.testTestFold`, plus the full PSI/non-PSI `LambdaGenerated` suites as regression guards.

## Non-exhaustive enum declaration flag and known-subject match narrowing

## Overload-by-lambda target-typed array literal candidate short-circuit

- problem type: `OverloadGenerated.testOverloadResolution3` spent unbounded time in overload-by-lambda candidate trials when a wrong candidate target-typed a deeply nested array literal and kept resolving all remaining elements after the first incompatible element.
- root cause: rollback analysis for overload-by-lambda candidates used the normal array-literal `transformChildren` path even when the expected array element type was already known. The wrong `(Int) -> Array<Component>` candidate failed on the first `Button(flag)` element but still recursively resolved later nested `Box { ... }` elements, repeatedly re-entering the same candidate-reduction path.

## Generic static interface member through implicit extend receiver

- problem type: `O2_part_gi.param_desugarDecl` resolved inherited static interface function `foo<T>` through the extend body's implicit receiver and then reported `ARGUMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` on the whole `extend<T> A<T> <: I<T>` declaration.
- root cause: `CfirCheckDispatchReceiver` treated the implicit receiver used to expose a static member scope as a runtime dispatch receiver and added a receiver subtype constraint. For `extend<T> A<T> <: I<T>`, that made the static interface member candidate `foo` compare type parameters from different declaration owners and surface a false receiver `ConstraintMismatch`.

A probe using `func foo<T>() { 1 }` as an `Int64` value also exited `0`, confirming the fixture's implicit function return was valid. Official implementation evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckReference.cpp` filters object member access to static members as an explicit object-access error, while `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp` `GetAllGenericTys` treats static member access as owner-generic inference input rather than an instance receiver subtype check.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/tower/FirTowerResolveTask.kt`, especially `toScopeBasedTowerLevelForStaticWithImplicitDispatchReceiver`, plus `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/ResolutionStages.kt` for dispatch receiver checking placement.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCheckDispatchReceiver.kt`.
- repair principle: keep owner generic substitution in the existing candidate fresh-variable initialization, but skip dispatch receiver subtype checking when a static callable is reached only through an implicit receiver used for scope lookup.

## Same-project macro package import usage through construction registry

- problem type: same-project macro package imports used only by construction-stage macro calls were falsely reported as `UNUSED_IMPORT` after macro expansion removed or replaced the original `@Macro` surface from final CFIR.
- root cause: `CfirImportsChecker` collected ordinary referenced names from final CFIR and tried to recover macro surface usage by reverse-mapping each surface source element to the current file path. That was path-stable for PSI but not for the light-tree raw builder, so non-PSI same-project macro imports lost their construction-only usage record.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/CheckUnusedImportImpl.cpp` `IsImportContentUsedInMacro` checks macro package imports against `importManager.GetUsedMacroDecls(*importSpec.curFile)`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Macro/MacroEvaluation.cpp` `SaveUsedMacros` records used macro declarations with `AddUsedMacroDecls`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Modules/ImportManager.cpp` owns `AddUsedMacroDecls` / `GetUsedMacroDecls`. This proves used macro calls are file-level import usage facts, not ordinary AST references after expansion.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/semantics/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/FirImportTrackerComponent.kt` and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/entrypoint/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/session/IncrementalPassThroughImportTrackerComponent.kt` as the session-component/import-tracking architecture reference; Kotlin has no Cangjie macro equivalent.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/providers/macro/MacroConstructionApi.kt`, `compiler/frontend/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/frontend/pipeline/MacroExpandPhase.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirImportsChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: record construction-consumed macro names in the session registry keyed by the same stable file identity used by macro cache keys, then let the shared imports checker query that file-level fact instead of depending on PSI/light-tree source reverse mapping.
- fixtures covered: `CfirAnalysisMacroTestGenerated` and `CfirAnalysisMacroPsiTestGenerated` same-project macro package methods: `testSameProjectMacroPackageDeclarationReference`, `testSameProjectMacroPackageExpressionRootPackage`, `testSameProjectMacroPackageExpressionAliasImport`, `testSameProjectMacroPackageImportOnly`, `testSameProjectMacroPackageExpressionAllUnderImport`, `testSameProjectMacroPackageExpression`, `testSameProjectMacroPackagePublicImportExpression`, and `testSameProjectMacroPackageExpressionAutoCompileDisabled`.

## Ordinary unused-import import target and light-tree grouped import regression

- problem type: the already-closed `UnusedImportGenerated` family regressed across PSI and non-PSI paths: unused all-under imports were skipped, `internal import` fixtures were treated as reexporting source imports, inherited/extension member usage did not always mark imported declaration targets as used, and light-tree grouped imports such as `std.collection.{ArrayList, Map}` lost the directive prefix and became unresolved bare names.
- root cause: `CfirImportsChecker` still used name-only unused-import accounting for several paths and skipped all-under imports before checking resolved usage facts. Source import reexport detection treated `internal import` like public/protected reexport at checker time. The light-tree raw builder also built each `IMPORT_ITEM` from the item-local expression only, unlike PSI `CjImportItem.importedFqName`, which composes the directive base path with grouped import items.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/CheckUnusedImportImpl.cpp` records used declaration targets and packages through `AddUsedTarget`, `AddUsedPackage`, and `CollectUsedPackages`, filters imports in `CollectNeedCheckImports`, and checks star and named imports through `IsImportContentUsed`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeChecker.cpp` calls `CheckUnusedImportSpec`. A direct `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all` probe for `internal import std.collection.ArrayList` exited `0` with no diagnostics, so the `internal import` branch here follows this repository's previously verified `UnusedImportGenerated` LLT surface rather than changing fixtures in the middle of the regression repair.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirImportsChecker.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirImportResolveTransformer.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/ImportingScopes.kt`; PSI grouping parity was checked against `psi/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/psi/CjImportDirectiveItem.kt` and `cfir/raw-cfir/psi2cfir/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/builder/PsiRawCfirBuilder.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirImportsChecker.kt`, `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/providers/CfirImportReexportInfo.kt`, and `cfir/raw-cfir/light-tree2cfir/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/lightTree/LightTreeRawCfirDeclarationBuilder.kt`.
- repair principle: keep unused-import decisions in the shared import checker using resolved target/package facts, keep source reexport classification in the provider helper, and make light-tree import construction match the PSI import model before import resolution instead of adding checker-side recovery for malformed FQNs.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `UnusedImportGenerated`, including ordinary `unusedImport001`, `unusedImport002`, `unusedImport003`, macro unused-import slices selected by the same generated-class filter, all-under import cases, internal import cases, inherited/extension member usage cases, and grouped import cases.

- verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; the focused PSI/non-PSI unused-import family completed with no failures.

## Qualified declaration macro import usage in PSI and light-tree macro LLT

- problem type: `macro.llt.unusedImport` package imports used only by qualified declaration macros such as `@macro_definition.ModifyFunc` and `@a.Derive[...]` were still reported as `UNUSED_IMPORT` on PSI, while the same construction-stage usage must keep the import live after macro expansion.
- root cause: the macro construction registry did not expose construction-consumed macro names as a file-level import usage fact, and the PSI top-level parser consumed only the first identifier after `@`, so qualified declaration macro surfaces never reached the PSI raw builder as the same `MACRO_EXPRESSION` shape that light-tree already used.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/CheckUnusedImportImpl.cpp` checks macro imports through `IsImportContentUsedInMacro` against `importManager.GetUsedMacroDecls(*importSpec.curFile)`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Macro/MacroCallResolve.cpp` resolves qualified macro names through imported package declarations; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Modules/ImportManager.cpp` owns the used-macro declaration table. This makes macro usage a per-file import fact, not an ordinary final-AST reference.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/semantics/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/FirImportTrackerComponent.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirImportResolveTransformer.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/ImportingScopes.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirImportsChecker.kt`; Kotlin is used only for import tracking/checker ownership because Cangjie macro semantics come from the official compiler.

## Catch parameter redeclaration scope in diagnostics2 try

- problem type: `diagnostics2/try` fixtures with repeated catch parameter names across separate catch clauses falsely reported `REDECLARATION` on the later catch parameter.
- root cause: the local redeclaration visitor did not open a separate local declaration scope for each `CfirCatch`, so catch pattern binding variables leaked into the enclosing function/block scope and conflicted with parameters from sibling catch clauses.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/include/cangjie/AST/Node.h` models `TryExpr` with parallel `catchPatterns` and `catchBlocks`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Collector.cpp` states that each catch block has the same scope as its catch pattern and calculates that scope per catch block/pattern pair.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/tree/gen/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/expressions/FirCatch.kt` and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirControlFlowStatementsResolveTransformer.kt`, where `transformCatch` enters the catch clause and resolves the parameter plus block inside a block context.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirConflictsDeclarationChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: model each catch clause as its own local declaration scope while sharing that scope between the catch parameter and catch body, instead of suppressing `REDECLARATION` for selected names or fixtures.
- fixtures covered: `diagnostics2/try/catchOrderingAndDuplicate.cj`, `diagnostics2/try/duplicateCatchPlaceholder.cj`, `diagnostics2/try/multiCatchJoinMismatch.cj`, `diagnostics2/try/tryMultipleCatchJoinMatrix.cj`, and `diagnostics2/try/unreachableCatchPlaceholder.cj` in PSI and non-PSI `TryGenerated`; `WithoutAliasExpansion` was also included in the focused run.

## Const-eval integer multiplication overflow and divisor-zero diagnostics

- problem type: `diagnostics/const-eval` and `diagnostics2/const-eval` failed to report `CONST_EVAL_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` for integer multiplication and failed to report `CONST_EVAL_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO` for literal `/ 0` and `% 0` expressions.
- root cause: `CfirConstEvalArithmeticChecker` excluded `TIMES` from the shared overflow-reporting operator set, and the divisor-zero branch skipped primitive literal calls whose callee reference was not a resolved named reference even though the shared primitive operator predicate could already prove the call was an integer primitive operator.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all cfir/analysis-tests/build/codex-probes/constEvalProbe.cj` reported `chir_arithmetic_operator_overflow` for both `9223372036854775807 + 1` and `9223372036854775807 * 2`, and `chir_divisor_is_zero` for both `10 / 0` and `10 % 0`. `external/cangjie_compiler/include/cangjie/CHIR/Analysis/ConstAnalysis.h` handles integer `ADD`, `SUB`, `MUL`, `DIV`, and `MOD` through `HandleArithmeticOpOfInt`, raises `RaiseDivByZeroError` when `DIV`/`MOD` right operand is zero, and maps `MUL`, `DIV`, and `MOD` in `RaiseArithmeticOverflowError`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/expression/FirDivisionByZeroChecker.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/expressions/FirExpressionEvaluator.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/frontend/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/resolve/constants/evaluate/ConstantExpressionEvaluator.kt`; Kotlin keeps division-by-zero and integer-overflow checks in constant-expression/operator evaluation owners.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirConstEvalArithmeticChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: keep constant integer arithmetic diagnostics in the shared const-eval arithmetic checker by using the same primitive-operator predicate for divisor-zero diagnostics and applying overflow range checks uniformly to multiplication as well as other integer arithmetic operators.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `CfirAnalysisDiagnosticsTest.diagnostics.const_eval.ConstEvalGenerated`, `CfirAnalysisDiagnosticsPsiTest.diagnostics.const_eval.ConstEvalGenerated`, `CfirAnalysisDiagnostics2Test.diagnostics2.const_eval.ConstEvalGenerated`, `CfirAnalysisDiagnostics2PsiTest.diagnostics2.const_eval.ConstEvalGenerated`, plus both `WithoutAliasExpansion` generated classes in the same const-eval slices.

## ClassGenerated constructor/member/static-global initialization flow

- problem type: constructor and member initialization flow in PSI and non-PSI `ClassGenerated`, including nested function/lambda capture before initialization, member calls before all instance fields are initialized, delegated constructor state, struct/member-initializer implicit receiver checks, same-file forward global reads from instance initializers, and binding-variable type projection needed by initializer diagnostics.
- root cause: `CfirInitializationCheckers` skipped anonymous/nested function bodies for capture-before-initialization, treated assignments inside nested functions as if they initialized the outer constructor state, did not model `this(...)` delegation as initializing instance fields after its arguments, over-skipped implicit struct member access in field initializers, and originally scanned all file-level static/global symbols from instance initializers instead of only top-level globals. `ReturnTypeCalculatorWithJump` could also fail when a `CfirPatternBindingVariable` requested its type before the owning pattern variable had projected binding types.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/CHIR/Checker/VarInitCheck.cpp` checks member function calls before all fields are initialized through `CheckMemberFuncCall`, `UseBeforeInitCheck`, and `RaiseIllegalMemberFunCallError`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp` reports `sema_undefined_variable`, `sema_capture_before_initialization`, `sema_class_uninitialized_field`, and `sema_illegal_usage_of_member`, and `IsVarUsedBeforeDefinition` distinguishes ordinary forward global references from class-like/static contexts. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/GlobalVarChecker.cpp` owns global/static initialization dependency collection. `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all cfir/analysis-tests/build/codex-probes/class_static_global_forward_static_member_probe.cj` accepted `A.a1 = B.b`, while `class_static_global_forward_global_probe.cj` reported `sema_undefined_variable` on `c` in `A.a = c`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/collectors/components/ControlFlowAnalysisDiagnosticComponent.kt`; Kotlin's FIR control-flow diagnostic component keeps initialization diagnostics attached to graph-owner/control-flow traversal rather than fixture-specific declaration checks.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/ReturnTypeCalculatorWithJump.kt`, and fixture range correction in `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/class/class_no_member_func_use_before_init4.cj`.

## ClassGenerated illegal interface super receiver recovery

- problem type: PSI and non-PSI `ClassGenerated` reported selector/call cascades after illegal `super` use inside interfaces: `interface_super_invalid_1.cj` produced `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` on `super.a()`, and `interface_super_invalid_2.cj` left `var c = super.a` without a callable function-value type so `c()` was reported unresolved.
- root cause: `CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.transformSuperReceiverExpression` used only `BodyResolveContext.containingRegularClass`, so `super` in an interface was typed as an unrecoverable error before member resolution. The error-node collector also only treated extend `super` as an illegal-owner cascade, so selector diagnostics after interface `super` were still emitted.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all cfir\analysis-tests\build\codex-probes\class_interface_super_probe.cj` reported exactly two `sema_use_super_in_interface` diagnostics, on `super.a()` and `let f = super.a`, with no unresolved selector or unresolved `f()`/`c()` diagnostics. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckReference.cpp` `TypeChecker::TypeCheckerImpl::CheckUsageOfSuper` gets the current inheritable declaration via `GetCurInheritableDecl`, reports `sema_use_super_in_interface` for `InterfaceDecl`, and leaves reference legality checking separate from name/member resolution.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, where `transformSuperReceiver` recovers `super` from the current implicit dispatch receiver's `superTypeRefs`; and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/collectors/components/ErrorNodeDiagnosticCollectorComponent.kt`, where unresolved diagnostics are skipped when the receiver cannot be resolved.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/BodyResolveContext.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/collectors/components/ErrorNodeDiagnosticCollectorComponent.kt`.
- repair principle: keep illegal-`super` legality in `CfirIllegalSuperReferenceChecker`, but let body resolve recover the current class-like owner and direct interface supertype for member typing, while the shared error collector suppresses selector cascades for all illegal `super` owner kinds.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt._class.ClassGenerated` / `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt._class.ClassGenerated` methods `testInterfaceSuperInvalid1` and `testInterfaceSuperInvalid2`.

- focused verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; both interface-super methods and the class `super` initializer guard passed in PSI and non-PSI paths.
- regression command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt._class.ClassGenerated' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt._class.ClassGenerated' --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --stacktrace --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache`

## ClassGenerated invisible member function diagnostic mapping

- problem type: PSI and non-PSI `ClassGenerated` mapped inaccessible member functions to the generic `INVALID_ACCESS_CONTROL` diagnostic instead of `INVISIBLE_MEMBER` for `class_static04.cj` and `class_access_control11.cj`.
- root cause: `ConeVisibilityError.mapConeVisibilityError` classified every inaccessible member callable as `INVALID_ACCESS_CONTROL`, even when the invisible symbol was a function. Official Cangjie distinguishes function access (`sema_invalid_access_function`) from non-function access (`sema_invalid_access_control`), and the repository already has `INVISIBLE_MEMBER` as the function-member diagnostic surface.

## ClassGenerated implicit Object super receiver for member-missing diagnostics

- problem type: PSI and non-PSI `ClassGenerated` reported `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` for `super.foo1()` when a class declared only interface supertypes, instead of reporting member absence from the official implicit `Object` superclass.
- root cause: `CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer` computed `super` receiver candidates only from declaration `superTypeRefs` filtered to concrete implementation types. Ordinary classes whose source declares only interfaces therefore had no receiver type, so member lookup created `ConeUnresolvedNameError` without a nominal receiver and diagnostic mapping could not produce `NOT_MEMBER_OF`.

## ClassGenerated member initializer self-name resolution

- problem type: PSI and non-PSI `ClassGenerated` treated a bare reference to the field currently being initialized as an initialized-member read diagnostic, and `class3.cj` had a stale missing marker for an actually undeclared initializer name.
- root cause: field initializers were resolved without a dedicated "current field initializer" context. A bare name such as `a` in `public var a = a` could therefore resolve through the class implicit receiver back to the field being declared, after which `CfirInitializationCheckers` reported `USED_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION`. Official Cangjie distinguishes this from explicit `this.a`: bare self-name lookup is unresolved, while explicit member access remains an initialization-flow diagnostic.

Implementation evidence is `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckReference.cpp`, where unresolved references report `sema_undeclared_identifier`, and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp` `CheckIllegalMemberAccess`, which owns explicit member initialization-flow diagnostics.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirMemberPropertiesChecker.kt` and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/collectors/components/ControlFlowAnalysisDiagnosticComponent.kt`, where property initialization and control-flow diagnostics are kept in initialization/CFA owners after resolve has already determined the referenced symbol.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/BodyResolveContext.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirDeclarationsResolveTransformer.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, and fixture correction in `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/class/class3.cj`.

## ClassGenerated class supertype list diagnostics

That prevented `C <: D` from reporting the official non-inheritable diagnostic on `D`, and it made diagnostics bind to the whole class source on the PSI path.

Implementation evidence is `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckClassLike.cpp` `TypeChecker::TypeCheckerImpl::CheckAndAddSubDecls`, which tracks `hasSuperClass` and `superClassLikeNum`, reports `sema_illegal_multi_inheritance`, `sema_superclass_must_be_placed_at_first`, and `sema_non_inheritable_super_class`, then records the concrete superclass.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirSupertypesChecker.kt`, where direct supertype-list legality is kept in one declaration checker after supertype resolution.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/checkers-component-generator/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/checkers/generator/diagnostics/CfirDiagnosticsList.kt`, `cfir/checkers/gen/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/CfirErrors.kt`, `cfir/checkers/gen/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/CfirNonSuppressibleErrorNames.kt`, `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/CfirErrorsDefaultMessages.kt`, `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirSupertypesChecker.kt`, and `cfir/analysis-tests/testFixtures/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/tests/golden/DiagnosticNameMapper.kt`.
- repair principle: implement the official supertype-list state machine in the shared class-like supertype checker and preserve the original delegated typeRef source behind resolve-stage error supertypes, so both raw-builder and PSI paths report the same official diagnostics on the written supertype token.

## ClassGenerated error-typed callable value invocation cascade

- problem type: PSI and non-PSI `ClassGenerated.testClassMissingTypeargumentsInvalid` reintroduced `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` on calls to `a(1)` and `b(1)` after `a` and `b` had already been given error function-value types from bare generic static member references.
- root cause: `CfirCallResolver.createResolvedNamedReference()` classified a successful named-value candidate used in a call position as generic unresolved when the value declaration's type was already `ConeErrorType`. That dropped the original bare-generic qualifier diagnostic and produced a second, misleading unresolved callee diagnostic at the later call site.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all cfir\analysis-tests\build\codex-probes\class_missing_typearguments_invalid_probe.cj` reported only two `sema_generic_type_without_type_argument` diagnostics for `let a = R.funca` and `var b = R.funca`; there were no later unresolved diagnostics for `a(1)` or `b(1)`. Implementation evidence remains `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckReference.cpp` for the bare generic member-access diagnostic and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeArgumentInference.cpp` `DiagnoseForCallInference` for actual call inference diagnostics.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/expression/FirPropertyAccessTypeArgumentsChecker.kt`, plus FIR call-resolution architecture where error-typed callees are propagated as error results instead of remapped to unrelated unresolved names.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt` and `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`.
- repair principle: when a call expression resolves its callee as a value whose declaration type is already a `ConeErrorType`, propagate that error through `ConeUnreportedDuplicateDiagnostic` instead of inventing a new unresolved-name diagnostic; this preserves the original semantic error owner and suppresses cascades for all equivalent callable-value recovery paths.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt._class.ClassGenerated.testClassMissingTypeargumentsInvalid` / `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt._class.ClassGenerated.testClassMissingTypeargumentsInvalid`.

## Function recursive-constructor dependency graph ordering and cycle-head selection

- problem type: recursive constructor diagnostics in `llt/function/recursive_ctor_00.cj` through `recursive_ctor_08.cj` must select the same dependency-cycle head as the official compiler and use the repository full-token range policy on constructor references.
- root cause: `CfirRecursiveConstructorCallChecker` treated a call whose target constructor was already visiting as a call-node cycle instead of re-entering the constructor node, resolved constructor owners only through the symbol provider during a phase where forward class-like declarations can still require the CFIR provider, and traversed raw CFIR declaration storage order where synthesized/primary constructors can precede source fields and secondary constructors. These divergences produced duplicate cross-type reports and selected call sites or primary constructors instead of the official cycle head.
- official Cangjie evidence: `C:\Users\lin17\.cangjie\sdks\cangjie-1.0.5\bin\cjc.exe --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all tmp\codex-function-recursive-constructor-probe.cj` reported exactly nine `sema_recursive_constructor_call` diagnostics: constructor references for direct/self field cycles, `init` declarations for constructor-delegation cycles, the implicit owner type for the superclass/field cycle, and the later dependency owner for cross-type cycles. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Utils.cpp` `CheckRecursiveCtorFoundCycle`, `DiagRecursiveConstructorCall`, and `CheckRecursiveConstructorCall` show the official graph vertices (`instance constructor` and `init reference`), constructor-reference-to-target edges, shared DFS path, and declaration-identifier versus reference-node range selection.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirCommonConstructorDelegationIssuesChecker.kt`, where constructor cycles are discovered through resolved delegated-constructor symbols and reported from the resolved delegated constructor call source.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirRecursiveConstructorCallChecker.kt`; range-only fixture corrections in `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/function/recursive_ctor_00.cj`, `recursive_ctor_03.cj`, and `recursive_ctor_05.cj`.
- repair principle: preserve the official constructor/reference dependency graph and semantic root order (`field initializers -> secondary constructors -> primary constructors`) in the shared checker so every PSI and light-tree fixture receives one deterministic cycle head without fixture-specific branching.
- fixtures covered: `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.function.FunctionGenerated` and `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.function.FunctionGenerated` methods `testRecursiveCtor00` through `testRecursiveCtor08`.

## Function struct mutability propagation and nested-instance capture

- problem type: immutable struct/extend members must propagate mutations through struct-valued receiver chains to the owning field, constructors and mut functions must use dedicated nested-instance capture diagnostics, and reference-type/Array chains must stop struct mutation propagation.
- root cause: `CfirImmutableFunctionCannotModifyFieldChecker` only recognized direct implicit/`this` field assignments, `CfirImmutableFunctionCannotAccessMutableFunctionChecker` only handled direct current-receiver calls, extend targets were not mapped back to their struct declaration, and the closest nested function was mistaken for the outer member function. The capture diagnostics `ILLEGAL_CAPTURE_THIS` and `CAPTURE_THIS_OR_INSTANCE_FIELD_IN_FUNC` were also absent from the CFIR diagnostic surface. Separately, `mut_function_09.cj` retained a stale property-write expectation and omitted the official immutable receiver mut-call diagnostic.

Exact probes `tmp\codex-function-mutability-08-exact.cj` and `tmp\codex-function-mutability-09-exact.cj` confirmed no diagnostic for `x[0] += 1` / `c.c += 1`, no property-body assignment diagnostic for `t1.t0 += 1`, and one `sema_immutable_access_mutable_func` for `a[0].t2.f()`. Official implementation was traced through `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckAccess.cpp` `CheckMutationInStructNonMut`, `CheckMutationInStruct`, and `CheckLetInstanceAccessMutableFunc`, plus `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr.cpp` / `TypeCheckReference.cpp` nested capture and immutable-member access checks.

## Indexed compound-assignment get/set type preservation

- problem type: ordinary Array/user-operator indexed compound assignments must retain the indexed `get` element type for operator checking while independently validating the `set` writeback call.
- root cause: `CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.transformAssignment` resolved the shared subscript node as the operator call receiver and correctly obtained its element type, then `resolveSubscriptSetAssignment` overwrote that same node with the `set` call's `Unit` return type. `CfirCompoundAssignmentSemanticsChecker` consequently interpreted `x[0] += 1` as `Unit += Int64` and emitted `TYPE_INCOMPATIBLE`.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc --diagnostic-format json --error-count-limit all tmp\codex-function-mutability-08-exact.cj` completed with no diagnostics for `x[0] += 1` or `c.c += 1`. Official compound/subscript assignment handling was traced through `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/AssignExpr.cpp` `InferAssignExprCheckCaseOverloading` / `SynAssignExpr` and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Desugar/DesugarInTypeCheck.cpp` subscript overload desugaring, which preserve the indexed value type while resolving writeback.

## Function-value overload selection and callable-reference diagnostics

- problem type: overloaded function names used as values must remain candidate-local through postponed completion, distinguish ambiguity from no matching declaration and missing generic type arguments, and select only candidates whose complete function type matches the target without Option auto-boxing.

Official `func_assign_var.cj` behavior reports no matching function declaration for reference on `x`, ambiguous use for `Sub().ff` and bare `a`, while a bare generic `foo` reference reports `sema_generic_type_without_type_argument`. Implementation evidence was traced through `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp` callable-reference checking, `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp` candidate matching, and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeManager.cpp` function-type compatibility.

## Constructor delegation argument-diagnostic ownership and failed-candidate recovery

- problem type: explicit `this(...)` and `super(...)` delegation must produce exactly one argument-count diagnostic from call resolution, select the official failed constructor candidate, and never turn an inapplicable candidate into a recursive-constructor dependency edge.

Completion subsequently converted that failed recovery candidate into a resolved reference, which created a false recursive-constructor edge, while constructor `TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS` source selection incorrectly treated constructors as ordinary functions and highlighted the whole call.

## Generic instantiation member-signature collisions

- problem type: generic class/struct/interface instantiation must report when previously distinct function members acquire identical parameter signatures, while valid inherited implementations must remain merged and diagnostic-free.

## Generic parent-constructor delegation substitution

- problem type: `this(...)` and `super(...)` delegation must resolve constructors through the complete instantiated target type, preserve already-fixed owner substitutions, and reject constructor signatures whose declaration-side parameter type is erroneous.

## Callable-reference completion with outer inference variables

- problem type: callable references used as arguments of an outer generic call must contribute constraints while the outer variables are unfixed, and a structural qualifier error must own its range without an additional derived no-match diagnostic.

Its failure mapper also inspected only an explicit receiver, missing the case where the failed argument itself was the erroneous bare generic qualifier.
- official Cangjie evidence: the previously established cjc 1.0.5 evidence for `instantiate_02.cj` requires filtering only after the resulting substitution is available; the function-composition fixtures are accepted, while `generic_call_static_impl11.cj` has only the bare-generic-classifier error.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/CheckCallableReferenceExpectedType.kt`, `FirCallResolver.kt`, and the FIR postponed-argument completion path.

- repair principle: postpone final nominal filtering while either side depends on outer unfixed variables, retain the resulting-substitutor filter once variables are fixed, and suppress a derived callable-reference no-match when the argument/qualifier subtree already carries the structural primary error.

- repair principle: classify accessor mutation context from the owning property's static contract, keeping getter/setter and ordinary static functions outside instance mutability propagation without changing static scope or completeness.

## Target-typed overloaded function references in generic enum payload calls

- problem type: overloaded function names used as payload arguments of a generic enum constructor must be resolved inside each outer candidate constraint-system branch, including explicit function type arguments, generic-overload exclusion, and outer argument-type ambiguity.

Completion then regenerated a callee-level `NO_CONSTRUCTOR` from the propagated argument failure.

## Qualified enum owner selection and Iterable protocol element extraction

- problem type: an explicit enum qualifier must determine the constructor owner even under a different expected enum type, and `for-in` element types must come from the concrete type's instantiated `Iterable<E>` supertype.

After that was corrected, `inferIterableElementType` still inspected only arrays, Range, or the concrete receiver's own first type argument; a non-generic `RGBColor` implementing `Iterable<RGBColor>` therefore produced an error loop-variable type.

CFIR's current dedicated for-in node uses the corresponding-supertype type-system seam until full convention-call desugaring is adopted.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/tower/TowerLevelHandler.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/ResolveUtils.kt`; and `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`.
- repair principle: expected enum owners refine only unqualified sugar, while protocol element types are read from the unique instantiated protocol supertype through the shared type checker rather than guessed from the concrete receiver shape.

## Local declaration initializer lookup excludes the declaration being introduced

With a top-level `class A2`, `var A2 = A2` resolves the RHS to the class and `TypeCheckReference.cpp:624-631` reports `sema_ref_not_be_type`; without the class, `NameReferenceExpr.cpp:426-441` and `EnumSugarTargetsFinder.cpp:24-63` continue to the zero-payload enum constructor.

## Distinct interface default implementations in inherited-member merging

- problem type: when different interfaces provide the same instantiated default-member signature, the derived class must retain both implementation origins and require an explicit implementation; duplicate paths to the same interface default must still merge.
- root cause: `CfirClassUseSiteMemberScope.mergeEquivalentInheritedFunctions()` keyed inherited functions only by static status plus pre- and post-substitution signatures. Distinct defaults such as `A.foo` and `B.foo` therefore collapsed to one symbol before `CfirNotImplementedOverrideChecker` could observe multiple interface owners.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_interface_member_must_be_implemented` on the derived class in `class_no_override_modifier_invalid_5/6/8.cj`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/MemberSignature.h:25`, `MergeInheritedMemberHelper.cpp:185-200`, and `StructInheritanceChecker.cpp:977-982` preserve multiple default origins through `shouldBeImplemented`; `DiagnosticSema.def:217` defines the diagnostic.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/AbstractFirUseSiteMemberScope.kt`, `FirTypeIntersectionScopeContext.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirNotImplementedOverrideChecker.kt` with `FirHelpers.getImplementationStatus()` / `AMBIGUOUSLY_INHERITED`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/scopes/impl/CfirClassUseSiteMemberScope.kt`.
- repair principle: preserve default implementation provenance in the shared inherited-function merge key, using the declaration owner only for default members so same-interface diamond paths still deduplicate while different interface defaults remain available to every downstream scope consumer.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `class_no_override_modifier_invalid_5.cj`, `_6.cj`, and `_8.cj`; `_7.cj` is the substitution/provenance guard and remained green.
- fixture correction: none.
- verification commands: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassNoOverrideModifierInvalid*' --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`; then both complete PSI/LT `ClassGenerated` suites.
- verification outcome: the focused family was `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; complete `ClassGenerated` XML reported 232 tests / 11 failures on each entry path, with `_5`, `_6`, `_7`, and `_8` all absent from the failure lists.

## Explicit callable type arguments and value-argument mismatch classification

- problem type: after explicit callable type arguments instantiate a function signature, value arguments must be checked against the substituted parameter types and reported as ordinary `TYPE_MISMATCH`, independently from type-argument arity and resolution errors.
- root cause: the central constraint-mismatch mapper did not distinguish callable-owned explicit type arguments from generic types appearing only on the receiver, so value-argument incompatibilities could use the wrong argument diagnostic category; stale fixtures also treated a type-position undeclared name as an expression unresolved reference.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckGeneric.cpp` `CheckCallGenericDeclInstantiation`, `CheckGenericDeclInstantiation`, and `GetGenericType` report generic-argument no-match only when the declaration/type-argument counts differ, then instantiate the callable through `GenerateTypeMapping` before checking values; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Diags.cpp:202,220` emits `sema_mismatched_types` for the resulting value mismatch. An independent cjc 1.0.5 probe for `data.getFoo<Roo<Int32>>(roo)` reported `sema_mismatched_types` on the complete `roo` range with expected `Roo<Roo<Int32>>` and actual `Roo<Int32>`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/TypeArgumentMapping.kt`, `CreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`, `CheckArguments.kt`, `ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/semantics/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/inference/model/FirConstraintPositionAndErrors.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`, plus fixture corrections in `function1.cj` and `class3.cj`.
- repair principle: identify explicit type arguments only when they belong to the selected callable, then let the shared substituted-parameter argument checker and central diagnostic mapper classify the value mismatch; receiver type arguments never masquerade as callable type arguments.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `function1.cj` and `class3.cj`; `class5_test.cj` remained the constructor analogue guard.
- fixture correction: `function1.cj` now expects `TYPE_MISMATCH` for `Add<Float64>(a)` and `UNDECLARED_TYPE_NAME` for type-position `T`; `class3.cj` includes the official `RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH`, `NO_VALUE_FOR_PARAMETER`, and both `TYPE_MISMATCH` expectations, including the explicit-callable-type-argument guard on `roo`.
- verification commands: the four-method critical Generics regression selecting `testFunction1`, `testClass3`, `testFunction14Test`, and `testGenericParameters2`; then both complete PSI/LT `GenericsGenerated` suites.
- verification outcome: the critical regression passed 8/8; the complete regression passed 296/296.

## Enum constructor value-domain flow and nested target typing

- problem type: local enum values constructed before a `match` must carry their exact constructor tag through assignments and control-flow joins, while nested same-name enum constructor calls must be resolved independently inside each outer candidate's expected-type branch.
- root cause: CFIR had no function-level enum constructor value-domain, so `UNREACHABLE_PATTERN` could not use constructor facts from local declarations; nested enum calls were also committed without candidate-local target typing. The initial repair exposed two framework defects: fixed fresh variables were still treated as constraint targets during same-classifier decomposition, and CHIR-derived value facts were consumed even when a Sema `NON_EXHAUSTIVE_MATCH` error would have stopped the official pipeline.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `chir_unreachable_pattern` for `enum12.cj`, `enum14.cj`, and `enum25_3.cj`. `TranslateCallExpr.cpp:635-675`, `ValueAnalysis.h:1334,1373,1386-1445`, `ConstAnalysis.cpp:543`, `UnreachableBranchCheck.cpp:57-162`, and `Engine.h:195-224` show enum constructor IDs flowing through CHIR value analysis. `EnumSugarTargetsFinder.cpp:24-83`, `TypeCheckCall.cpp:1165-1179,1365-1405,1957-2005,2014,2096-2143,2750-2774`, and `TypeChecker.cpp:509-523,1065-1075,1228` show nested arguments checked under each candidate's parameter type and committed only after candidate selection. For `enum28.cj`, cjc reports only `sema_nonexhuastive_patterns`; `CompileStrategy.cpp:572-588` proves that this Sema error prevents CHIR unreachable analysis. Enum constructor identity is declaration/ordinal based in `TranslateCallExpr.cpp:650-657` and `TranslateMatchExpr.cpp:251`, so same-name constructors remain distinct by payload arity.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `FirDataFlowAnalyzer.kt:1097-1108`, `FirLocalVariableAssignmentAnalyzer.kt:151-203,268-294`, FIR DFA symbol-value modeling, `FirWhenExhaustivenessComputer.kt`, `NewConstraintSystemImpl.fixVariable`, `ConstraintInjector.kt`, and `InferenceUtils.buildCurrentSubstitutor`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `CfirMatchSubjectValueDomainData.kt`, `CfirEnumTagFlowAnalyzer.kt`, `CfirDataFlowAnalyzer.kt`, `CfirLocalVariableAssignmentAnalyzer.kt`, `CfirMatchUnreachablePatternChecker.kt`, `ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, `CfirCallCompleter.kt`, and `Candidate.kt`.
- repair principle: preserve exact constructor facts and callable write effects in a function-level DFA carrier, resolve nested enum calls in isolated outer-candidate contexts, and only inject constraints into variables still present in `notFixedTypeVariables` after applying the current fixed-variable substitutor.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum12.cj`, `enum14.cj`, and `enum25_3.cj`; regression guards included `enum13.cj`, `enum15.cj`, `enum16_1.cj`, `enum28.cj`, and `enum32_1.cj`.
- fixture correction: none.
- verification commands: the combined PSI/LT focused regression selecting `testEnum12`, `testEnum13`, `testEnum14`, `testEnum15`, `testEnum161`, `testEnum253`, `testEnum28`, and `testEnum321`; then both complete PSI/LT `llt.enum.EnumGenerated` classes.
- verification outcome: the focused regression passed 16/16. The complete Enum regression ran 138 tests with 24 failures across 12 PSI/LT-symmetric fixtures; `enum12`, `enum13`, `enum14`, `enum25_3`, and `enum28` were absent from the failure list, with no new regression.

## Candidate-bearing nested enum calls and ambiguity dominance

- problem type: nested same-named enum constructor calls must remain candidate-local until the outer call selects a branch; when every successful outer ambiguity branch independently explains the same nested call, the outer ambiguity structurally dominates the inner ambiguity diagnostic without choosing an inner winner.
- root cause: speculative nested resolution completed and mutated shared call trees too early, literal types were reused after candidate-specific concretization, enum constructors exposed declaration return types instead of substituted owner enum types, and the first ambiguity-dominance implementation permanently replaced the original nested call diagnostic/type with an unreported wrapper.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 accepts `Out(Day(Year(3)))`; for `Day(Year(1))` across two enum owners it reports only the outer `sema_multiple_constructor_in_enum`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:1165-1179,1957-2005,2096-2143,2583-2606` checks nested calls under each outer candidate target and classifies the final enum-constructor ambiguity without committing an arbitrary branch.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: Kotlin FIR `ConeResolutionAtoms.kt`, `CandidateFactory.kt`, `CheckArguments.kt`, `FirCallResolver.kt`, and `FirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt` for candidate-bearing nested atoms, subsystem merging, and winner-only recursive completion.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/candidate/Candidate.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/CfirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/ResolveUtils.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt`, `cfir/semantics/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/diagnostic/ConeDiagnostic.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/collectors/components/ErrorNodeDiagnosticCollectorComponent.kt`.
- repair principle: speculative resolution owns detached candidate state and immutable dominance metadata; only the selected outer candidate writes replacements, while diagnostic collection suppresses an inner ambiguity solely when the containing outer ambiguity carrier references that exact diagnostic object.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum14.cj` and `enum14_1.cj`; guards included `enum10.cj`, `enum13.cj`, `enum28.cj`, and the complete Enum generated slice.
- verification commands: focused `*EnumGenerated.testEnum14` plus `*EnumGenerated.testEnum141`; then `:cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*llt.enum.EnumGenerated*' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- verification outcome: focused PSI/LT `enum14` and `enum14_1` passed 4/4; the complete Enum slice ran 142 tests with 20 failures across 10 unrelated PSI/LT-symmetric fixtures, and both repaired fixtures were absent from the failure list.

## Target-typed Rune literal conversion diagnostics

- problem type: a Rune literal that cannot convert to its contextual target type must report the dedicated `CANNOT_CONVERT_LITERAL` diagnostic in calls, declarations, default values, ranges, and other shared target-typing consumers.
- root cause: Rune literals were typed as `Rune`, then every incompatible target was flattened into the caller-specific `ARGUMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` or `TYPE_MISMATCH`; the shared mismatch classifier had no access to the original literal expression and the project diagnostic surface lacked `CANNOT_CONVERT_LITERAL`.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_cannot_convert_literal` with `cannot convert a character literal to type 'Int32'` for both `TimeUnit.Month(r'a')` and an ordinary function parameter. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/LitConstExpr.cpp:113-127,193-209` routes Rune target checking through `ChkLitConstExprOfTypeChar`, and `TypeChecker.cpp:1122-1135` applies target-typed literal checking independently of call kind.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: Kotlin FIR `ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, `coneDiagnosticToFirDiagnostic.kt`, and `IntegerLiteralAndOperatorApproximationTransformer.kt` for separating literal typing from call-argument diagnostic mapping; the Cangjie-specific literal-conversion classification comes only from official Cangjie evidence.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/checkers-component-generator/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/checkers/generator/diagnostics/CfirDiagnosticsList.kt`, `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/CfirErrorsDefaultMessages.kt`, `CfirTypeSemanticsDiagnostics.kt`, `coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`, and the shared initializer/range/try mismatch callers; fixture corrections in `enum10.cj`, `depth_call.cj`, and `var_literal_type_incompatible.cj`.
- repair principle: preserve the original literal expression at the shared mismatch-classification seam and emit a parameterized literal-conversion diagnostic before context-specific generic mismatch diagnostics.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum10.cj`, `depth_call.cj`, and `var_literal_type_incompatible.cj`.
- verification commands: focused LT `EnumGenerated.testEnum10`; focused PSI `EnumGenerated.testEnum10` with both `testEnum141` guards; `*FunctionGenerated.testDepthCall`; and `*VarGenerated.testVarLiteralTypeIncompatible`.
- verification outcome: `enum10`, `depth_call`, and `var_literal_type_incompatible` all passed on PSI and LightTree; the complete Enum slice also omitted `enum10` from its 20 remaining failures.

## Arity-only failed-candidate selection and qualified-call argument ranges

- problem type: argument-count diagnostics must select the overload whose accepted arity best explains the call, mark a concrete extra argument when one exists, and mark only the selector call's parenthesized argument list for missing parameters on qualified calls.
- root cause: ordinary calls did not reuse the arity-distance reduction already present for delegating constructors, so a one-parameter enum candidate could become the representative error for a three-argument call even when a two-parameter candidate was closer. Separately, PSI and LightTree `VALUE_ARGUMENTS`/`VALUE_ARGUMENTS_LIST` positioning recognized only root call nodes and fell back to the entire qualified expression.
- official Cangjie evidence: range-only repair; the project Diagnostic Range Policy is authoritative. Across the repository, concrete extra arguments are marked individually, while `NO_VALUE_FOR_PARAMETER` normally covers the callee selector's complete parenthesized argument list.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: Kotlin FIR `FirArgumentsToParametersMapper.kt:208-211,249-266,302-313`, `coneDiagnosticToFirDiagnostic.kt:213-226`, and `FirDiagnosticsList.kt:756-761`; Kotlin stores the actual extra argument and uses a value-arguments positioning strategy for missing parameters.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt`, `common/diagnostics/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/diagnostics/PositioningStrategies.kt`, and `LightTreePositioningStrategies.kt`; fixture range correction in `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/enum/enum1.cj`.
- repair principle: choose the most explanatory pure-arity failure before normal most-specific reduction, then let shared diagnostics positioning derive ranges from the actual extra argument or the selector-side argument list instead of reconstructing ranges in the converter.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum16_2.cj`, `enum1_optionalBITOR.cj`, and `enum1.cj`; repository search found 26 `TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS` markers and 30 `NO_VALUE_FOR_PARAMETER` markers as the wider guard family.
- verification commands: focused `*EnumGenerated.testEnum162` plus `*EnumGenerated.testEnum1OptionalBITOR`; complete `*llt.enum.EnumGenerated*` rerun; focused guard rerun selecting `testEnum1`, `testEnum162`, and `testEnum1OptionalBITOR`.
- verification outcome: the two triggering fixtures passed on PSI and LightTree; the complete Enum slice dropped from 20 to 18 failures and neither trigger remained. The only newly exposed difference was the stale whole-call range in `enum1.cj`; after correcting it to the shared argument-list policy, the six-test PSI/LT guard passed.

## Bare generic enum/static calls and ideal-literal inference

- problem type: a static member declared on a generic enum or its `extend` must infer the bare owner type arguments from the selected extension target, while ideal numeric literals inside a partially inferred generic call must contribute their concrete default primitive type soon enough for builtin operator resolution.
- root cause: fresh-variable creation treated every bare generic owner uniformly, losing the concrete `extend E<Rune>` relay from the enum owner parameter to the extension parameter; ideal-literal constraints were also recorded as unresolved `LOWER(IdealInt)` bounds, so a nested generic call operand had no stable primitive type when the builtin `+` fast path ran.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 accepts `enum36.cj` without diagnostics and accepts `enum45_generic_extend_staticFunc.cj` with only the unused-variable warning. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:192+` collects generic parameters for static members reached through a bare generic owner; `MultiTypeSubstUtils.cpp:360+` uses `GenerateTypeMapping` and `RelayMappingFromExtendToExtended` to connect extension parameters to the extended type; `LocalTypeArgumentSynthesis.cpp:558-590,1058+` adds ideal-literal constraints and applies `ResetIdealTypesInSubst` before final use.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: Kotlin FIR call-resolution fresh-variable creation, argument constraint generation, constraint-system completion, and builtin operator resolution paths corresponding to `CreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`, `ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, and expression resolution.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, and `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`.
- repair principle: construct the owner/extension substitution graph at candidate creation, normalize ideal literals to evidence-backed primitive bounds at the shared argument-constraint seam, and expose only a unique primitive bound to builtin operator lookup without fixing variables or mutating the nested call.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum36.cj` and `enum45_generic_extend_staticFunc.cj`.
- fixture correction: none.
- verification commands: `.\\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --rerun --tests '*EnumGenerated.testEnum36' --tests '*EnumGenerated.testEnum45GenericExtendStaticFunc' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 7m 32s`; all four PSI/LightTree tests passed.

- problem type: an accessor body that can complete normally without a value must be checked against its declared getter return type, and assignment to an immutable qualified property must report on the complete lvalue rather than only the terminal selector.

- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_type_mismatch` for `get() {}` together with `sema_immutable_property_with_setter`, and reports `sema_cannot_assign_to_immutable` on both complete property assignments in `enum17_prop2.cj`.
