- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `FirFunctionReturnTypeMismatchChecker.kt`, `FirReassignmentAndInvisibleSetterChecker.kt`, and the PSI/LightTree raw FIR accessor builders that propagate accessor return types.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirFunctionBodyTypeMismatchChecker.kt` and `CfirAssignmentLegalityChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: model normal block completion as `Unit` at the shared function-body checker and derive immutable-assignment ranges from the lvalue expression owned by the assignment checker.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum17_prop2.cj`.
- fixture correction: none.
- verification commands: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --rerun --tests '*EnumGenerated.testEnum17Prop2' --tests '*EnumGenerated.testEnum301' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.

## Declared generic upper bounds use strict subtype relations

- problem type: use-site validation of a declared generic upper bound must not treat expression-level `T -> Option<T>` promotion as satisfying the bound; an illegal enum upper-bound declaration still participates in explicit type-argument constraint checking.
- root cause: fresh-variable initialization correctly added `α <: Option<B>` and explicit `test<B>()` added `α == B`, but constraint incorporation checked the derived proper constraint `B <: Option<B>` with the ordinary subtype state, whose Option auto-boxing returned true. The post-resolve upper-bound checker repeated the same permissive comparison, so no solver or checker diagnostic was produced.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports both `sema_upper_bound_must_be_class_or_interface` on `T` and `sema_generic_type_argument_not_match_constraint` on explicit `B` in `enum26_1.cj`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/PreCheck.cpp:1036-1057` diagnoses the illegal bound kind without disabling later use-site checking, and `TypeCheckGeneric.cpp:250-275` validates the actual type argument against the declared bound.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/CreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/FirUpperBoundViolatedHelpers.kt`, `FirUpperBoundViolatedQualifiedAccessExpressionChecker.kt`, and `FirUpperBoundViolatedTypeChecker.kt`; solver and checker consume the same resolved bounds.
- CFIR owner files changed: `common/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/type/AbstractTypeChecker.kt`; `resolution.common/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/resolve/calls/inference/components/ConstraintInjector.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCreateFreshTypeVariableSubstitutorStage.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/CfirCallCompleter.kt`; `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/providers/CfirExtendSubstitution.kt`; `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/CfirUpperBoundViolatedHelpers.kt`; `CfirGenericInstantiationChecker.kt`; and `coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`.

## Concrete generic type-pattern reachability without Option promotion

- problem type: concrete sealed-like generic types with the same classifier but different invariant arguments must be recognized as disjoint type patterns; an unreachable type-pattern row must not cover a later wildcard.
- root cause: `AbstractTypeChecker` performed Option auto-boxing before same-constructor invariant argument comparison, so `Option<Int64> <: Option<Option<Int64>>` incorrectly returned true. `convertPattern` therefore downgraded the first type pattern to a wildcard before Maranget analysis, added it to `previousRows`, and made the following wildcard unreachable.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_unreachable_pattern` on `case _: Option<Option<Int64>>` for an `Option<Int64>` selector while the following `_` remains reachable. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/PatternUsefulness.cpp:92-123,469-511,603-613,847-862,1020-1053` computes a witness intersection and does not add a witness-less row to the preceding matrix.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirWhenExhaustivenessComputer.kt` and `FirControlFlowStatementsResolveTransformer.kt`; branch coverage is accumulated from the actual subject-domain intersection rather than every syntactic branch.
- CFIR owner files changed: `common/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/type/AbstractTypeChecker.kt`; `cfir/semantics/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/match/CfirMatchTypeRelations.kt`; `cfir/semantics/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/match/exhaustive/inria/MarangetChecker.kt`; and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirMatchUnreachablePatternChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: use the strict no-Option-promotion subtype relation at every type-pattern ordinary-subtype seam, treat only unresolved generic components as open shapes, and add only reachable unguarded rows to coverage state.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `enum.cj`; guards included `PatternMatching/Sealed/exhaustive_interface.cj`, `TypePattern/unreachable_simple.cj`, `unreachable_nothing.cj`, `type11.cj`, `exhaustive_generic.cj`, and `Sealed/sealed_open_unreachable.cj`. The wider guard run identified an independent diagnostic-range mismatch in `non_exhaustive_generic.cj` and pre-existing path-specific issues in `match024.cj`.
- fixture correction: none.
- verification commands: focused six-test command selecting `testEnum`, `testEnum2`, and `testEnum261`; then the clean combined guard command selecting the six listed type-pattern guards on both PSI/LT entry paths.
- verification outcome: `enum.cj` passed in the six-test run; the clean combined guard set passed with `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3m 50s`.

## Internal unused-import checking follows no-sub-package compilation mode

- problem type: `internal import` participates in unused-import diagnostics only when the source package is compiled with `--no-sub-pkg`; when it participates, usage is collected across the whole package rather than only the importing file.
- root cause: CFIR treated every non-public/protected `internal import` as an unused-import candidate regardless of package compilation mode. The checker already had package-wide usage collection for internal imports, but the configuration and session layers did not carry the official `noSubPkg` mode, so default-mode imports such as `enum43_import.cj` were falsely reported unused.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports no diagnostics for `enum43_import.cj` by default and reports one `sema_unused_import` for `std.convert.*` with `--no-sub-pkg`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Option/OptionAction.cpp:659` sets the option, `src/Frontend/CompilerInstance.cpp:306-313` writes it to the source package, `include/cangjie/AST/Node.h:2847-2853` defines re-export behavior by `noSubPkg`, and `src/Sema/CheckUnusedImportImpl.cpp:87-112,139-173,210-286` excludes public/protected imports, excludes internal imports only when `noSubPkg` is false, and selects package-wide usage for non-private imports. `src/Parse/ParseImports.cpp:113-163` explains the per-item diagnostics for grouped imports.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirImportsChecker.kt`, `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirImportResolveTransformer.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/entrypoint/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/session/FirAbstractSessionFactory.kt`; Kotlin compiler has no unused-import diagnostic, so its IDE `K2OptimizeImportsFacility.kt` and `KotlinUnusedImportInspection.kt` were consulted only for ownership separation, while the session setting-holder pattern came from `FirLookupDefaultStarImportsInSourcesSettingHolder.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/entrypoint/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/entrypoint/configuration/CfirFrontendConfigurationKeys.kt`, `cfir/cfir-tree/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/session/CfirLanguageSettingsComponent.kt`, `cfir/entrypoint/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/entrypoint/session/CfirAbstractSessionFactory.kt`, `tests/test-infrastructure/testFixtures/org/cangnova/cangjie/test/directives/CfirDiagnosticsDirectives.kt`, `tests/test-infrastructure/testFixtures/org/cangnova/cangjie/test/services/EnvironmentConfigurator.kt`, `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/providers/CfirImportReexportInfo.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirImportsChecker.kt`; fixture corrections add `// NO_SUB_PKG` to all files under `unusedImport003` and `unusedImport004`.
- repair principle: carry package compilation mode through the shared configuration-to-session chain and let the import semantic helper decide unused-check exemption, while preserving internal import's same-package visibility and package-wide usage accounting in both modes.

## Shared receiver DAG evaluation in local-assignment mini CFG

- problem type: deeply nested resolved unary-operator calls must be traversed linearly by the local-assignment mini CFG even when each call stores the same operand object in both explicit and dispatch receiver slots.
- root cause: `MiniCfgBuilder.visitFunctionCall` unconditionally visited `explicitReceiver` and `dispatchReceiver`. Completed unary calls legitimately share one CFIR receiver DAG node between those slots, so a chain of roughly 64 unary calls expanded as `T(n) = 2*T(n-1)` and kept the PSI `timeout_06` test at high CPU for hours.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 compiled `timeout_06.cj` successfully with 0 diagnostics in 1393 ms. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:1365-1408,1596-1608,1960-2011,2096-2143` checks an untyped lambda separately against each overload candidate with suppressed diagnostics; `src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/LambdaExpr.cpp:311-405` injects the candidate function type and safely rechecks the lambda; `src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/UnaryExpr.cpp:73-98` and `src/Sema/Desugar/DesugarInTypeCheck.cpp:322-344` process each unary node once and reuse an existing desugared call on re-entry.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/dfa/FirLocalVariableAssignmentAnalyzer.kt`, whose `MiniCfgBuilder.visitFunctionCall` deduplicates explicit, dispatch, and extension receivers before visiting; Kotlin generated `FirFunctionCallImpl.kt` and CFIR generated `CfirFunctionCallImpl.kt` also guard receiver traversal by object identity.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/dfa/CfirLocalVariableAssignmentAnalyzer.kt`.
- repair principle: preserve the custom call evaluation order while evaluating each shared receiver DAG node exactly once by object identity; do not add a global visited set that could hide illegal cycles or discard context-sensitive flow traversal.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `timeout_00.cj`, `timeout_01.cj`, `timeout_03.cj`, `timeout_04.cj`, `timeout_06.cj`, `timeout_07.cj`, plus `operator/unary_overload.cj` as the ordinary unary-overload guard.
- fixture correction: none.
- family verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --rerun --tests '*operator_overload.OperatorOverloadGenerated.testTimeout*' --tests '*operator.OperatorGenerated.testUnaryOverload' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- family verification outcome: all 14 PSI/LightTree tests completed in `6m 58s`, proving the hang was removed. `timeout_03`, `timeout_04`, `timeout_06`, and `unary_overload` passed on both entry paths; only the pre-existing expectation mismatches in `timeout_00`, `timeout_01`, and `timeout_07` failed on both paths.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --rerun --tests '*operator_overload.OperatorOverloadGenerated.testTimeout06' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- focused verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 40s`; both PSI and LightTree `timeout_06` tests passed.

## Nested return-type overload refinement reuses immutable tower discovery

- problem type: deeply nested calls whose overloads share the same parameter shape but differ by concrete return type must be refined by the outer parameter type without replaying full tower discovery at every nesting level.
- root cause: `ArgumentCheckingProcessor.resolveNestedCallForExpectedType` rebuilt a copied call and invoked the complete tower resolver for every outer candidate and every nested level. Although an early expected-return stage stopped incompatible candidates before their arguments, the root call still created eight candidate chains, each level rediscovered the same overload symbols, and `CfirResolutionSnapshot` repeatedly traversed the remaining nested subtree. Concrete primitive subtype checks also entered the general corresponding-supertype BFS before the shared type system recognized that different primitive kinds are final and unrelated.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 compiles `overload_resolution_2.cj` with zero diagnostics in about 1128 ms. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:1165-1198,1365-1408,1957-2011,2096-2143` discovers the function declaration list once, checks each `FunctionCandidate` with candidate-local constraint checkpoints and the target return type, then reapplies only the selected candidate's argument inference. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeManager.cpp:958-990,1000+` handles ordinary primitive subtype relations by exact primitive kind before interface/extend traversal, with separate rules for ideal literals and `Nothing`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`, `ConeResolutionAtoms.kt`, `candidate/CandidateFactory.kt`, `FirCallResolver.kt`, and `inference/FirCallCompleter.kt`; Kotlin keeps nested candidate atoms and subsystem storage, separates tower discovery from fresh candidate state, and applies the outer expected type through the candidate/completion pipeline rather than redoing name lookup.
- CFIR owner files changed: `common/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/type/AbstractTypeChecker.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/ExpectedTypeCompatibility.kt`; `calls/candidate/CfirCallableCandidateDiscovery.kt`; `CfirCandidateCollector.kt`; `CandidateFactory.kt`; `CallKind.kt`; `calls/stages/CfirCheckExpectedReturnTypeBeforeArguments.kt`; `ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`; and `body/CfirCallResolver.kt`.
- repair principle: keep tower discovery as immutable call-node metadata, deduplicate the same declaration discovered through equivalent file/package scopes, and create a completely fresh candidate only when all return shapes are deterministic and the outer expected type selects a unique target; never reuse an old candidate's system, stage progress, diagnostics, or replacements.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `overload_resolution_2.cj`; `overload_resolution_1.cj` through `overload_resolution_5.cj` were run as the neighboring overload guard family.
- fixture correction: none.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --rerun --tests '*overload.OverloadGenerated.testOverloadResolution2' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- focused verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 4m 16s`; XML recorded PSI `testOverloadResolution2` in 7.174 s and LightTree in 1.044 s, both with zero failures and errors. The previous 15-minute high-CPU blocker no longer reproduces.
- family verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --rerun --tests '*overload.OverloadGenerated.testOverloadResolution*' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- family verification outcome: all 10 PSI/LightTree tests completed in 1m15s. `overload_resolution_2`, `_4`, and `_5` passed on both entry paths; `_1` has an independent diagnostic-range mismatch (`ConsTest.f` versus selector-only `f`), and `_3` has an independent unresolved function-value invocation in constructor bodies. Neither remaining family failure is a timeout or nested expected-return refinement failure.

## Expected-return discovery is body-resolve transaction state

- problem type: immutable overload discovery retained for nested expected-return refinement must not keep completed call trees alive for the entire CFIR session.
- root cause: `CfirCallResolver` is session-owned through the body-resolve processor, while its identity map strongly retained call nodes and discovery values containing symbol, scope, and receiver graphs; no transaction boundary cleared the map after a file body finished resolving.
- official Cangjie evidence: this is a CFIR lifecycle correction rather than a language-semantic divergence; the already recorded `TypeCheckCall.cpp:1957-2011,2096-2143` evidence establishes candidate-local reuse only within one call-check transaction, not a compiler-session cache.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/FirCallResolver.kt`, `calls/candidate/CandidateFactory.kt`, and `transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`; candidate/discovery state is owned by the active resolution transaction and is not stored as an unbounded session map.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt` and `CfirAbstractBodyResolveTransformer.kt`.
- repair principle: keep identity-based discovery alive for nested re-resolution inside one file body transaction, then clear it unconditionally in the outer `transformFile` `finally` boundary; do not replace it with a weak-key map whose values can retain the keys through scope/symbol graphs.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `overload_resolution_2.cj`; the lifecycle boundary applies to every body-resolved file.
- fixture correction: none.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests "org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.overload.OverloadGenerated.testOverloadResolution2" --tests "org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.overload.OverloadGenerated.testOverloadResolution2" -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain`.
- verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 41s`; both PSI and LightTree focused tests passed after transaction cleanup.

## Variable-backed function values use the shared implicit-invoke path

- problem type: function values stored in enum payloads and recovered through match bindings must be callable from the branch body, just like parameters and ordinary local variables.
- root cause: the match binding was correctly registered and typed as `(Int32) -> Int32`, but the first direct-call attempt produced `ConeInapplicableCandidateError` for a `CfirPatternBindingSymbol`. Implicit-invoke recovery accepted that diagnostic only for enum constructors, and its declaration-type recovery was limited to `CfirValueParameterSymbol`, so variable-backed function values were left as `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 compiles `enum11_1.cj` successfully (exit 0; only the independent unused-parameter warning). `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:2536-2578,2839-2890,2908-2989` classifies non-declaration call bases separately and invokes `CheckFuncPtrCall` whenever the base expression type can be cast to `FuncTy`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/FirCallResolver.kt:120-145`, `calls/tower/FirInvokeResolveTowerExtension.kt:130-218`, and `calls/candidate/CallInfo.kt`; Kotlin first resolves any callable receiver candidate, calculates its return type, then creates a common implicit-`invoke` call instead of restricting receiver ownership to value parameters or enum entries.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt` and `CfirCallResolver.kt`.
- repair principle: classify every `CfirVariableSymbol` as a valid implicit-invoke receiver candidate, recover the declaration-side type through the shared variable-symbol abstraction, and keep enum-pattern constructor probing diagnostic-free when the bare name is actually a binding.

## Nested functions in member initializers preserve object-initialization semantics

- problem type: a local function or its default parameter declared inside an instance-field initializer must not access current-class or inherited instance members before object initialization completes.
- root cause: the shared initialization analyzer entered nested function bodies but skipped value-parameter defaults, classified every nested access as a local capture, and required the individual field to still be uninitialized. Resolution also failed to prepare signatures for functions syntactically nested in class member initializers and did not register such local functions because the outer container was a class, causing value-parameter return-type exceptions and unresolved sibling local-function references.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_illegal_usage_of_member` for the five current-class accesses in `variable_use_before_init.cj` and the struct access in `capture_func_record_3601.cj`; it reports `sema_illegal_usage_of_super_member` for both default-parameter accesses in `localfuncinvarinit.cj` and the inherited access in `capture_super_member.cj`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp:413-428,1481-1548` checks parameter defaults and forbids member/super-member capture while the object is being initialized.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/cfa/VariableInitializationCheckProcessor.kt`, `FirPropertyInitializationAnalyzer.kt`, `analysis/cfa/util/PropertyInitializationInfoCollector.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/dfa/cfg/ControlFlowGraphBuilder.kt`; Kotlin keeps nested graph ownership and member-initializer evaluation context in shared CFA rather than treating every nested access as the same capture kind.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirDeclarationsResolveTransformer.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/BodyResolveContext.kt`.
- repair principle: classify tracked declarations by semantic storage kind, analyze nested defaults before the body, preserve member-initializer object state across nested functions, and use declaration locality—not merely the outer container kind—to prepare and register local function signatures.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `localfuncinvarinit.cj`, `variable_use_before_init.cj`, `capture_func_record_3601.cj`, and `capture_super_member.cj` (18 expected diagnostic points across both entry paths).

## Constructor completeness checks every normal return exit

- problem type: an instance constructor that returns before all required fields are initialized must be rejected even when another branch or the lexical function end initializes the fields.
- root cause: initialization analysis collapsed control flow to one end state. A `return` only set `terminated = true`, branch merge discarded that terminated path, and constructor completeness skipped a terminated end state entirely, so early-return exits never participated in definite assignment.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_class_uninitialized_field` for both constructors in `variable_assignment_terminated_in_ctor_01.cj` and only the conditionally returning first constructor in `_02.cj`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp:313-350,1600-1657` records the uninitialized-member snapshot at each constructor `return` and combines it with the ordinary body exit.

- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`.
- repair principle: retain reachable explicit-return initialization snapshots by target-function identity, combine them with a non-terminated lexical end, and report each field once when any constructor exit leaves it uninitialized; nested-function returns remain outside the constructor exit set.

## Multiple assignment owns tuple compatibility and suppresses derived condition errors

- problem type: tuple multiple assignment must evaluate the complete RHS before writes, initialize every target represented by the desugared assignments, report only the first tuple shape/type incompatibility on the complete RHS, and prevent that root error from cascading into an outer `if`/loop condition mismatch.
- root cause: initialization analysis treated tuple lvalues as reads and continued traversing sibling operands after the first initialization diagnostic; resolve then modeled every assignment as a successful `Unit` expression, while the ordinary assignment checker compared the two tuple types as one normal assignment. This produced a left-side `Bool <- Unit` condition mismatch plus a right-side `ASSIGNMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH`, with overlapping ranges, instead of one multiple-assignment root diagnostic.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports exactly one `sema_mismatched_types_multiple_assign` on each `(1, 2, 3)` RHS in `variable_use_before_init_03.cj`, and that mismatch plus only the first later uninitialized `b` in `_04.cj`; `_02.cj` reports only its three first reachable uninitialized `b` reads. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/AssignExpr.cpp:93-131,310-325` performs recursive tuple shape/type checking with first-error return and suppresses diagnostics from synthesizing the original tuple lvalue; `TypeCheckExpr/Diags.cpp:12-18` anchors the primary diagnostic on the RHS and keeps the LHS as a secondary hint; `Desugar/DesugarBeforeTypeCheck.cpp:309-345` evaluates the whole RHS into a temporary before left-to-right writes; `LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp:862-909,1005-1007,1326-1333` analyzes the desugared writes and short-circuits tuple/binary initialization diagnostics after the first failure.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: Kotlin FIR `FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, `FirAssignmentTypeMismatchChecker.kt`, `FirHelpers.checkTypeMismatch`, `FirDataFlowAnalyzer.kt`, `FirDestructuringDeclarationChecker.kt`, and `ErrorNodeDiagnosticCollectorComponent.kt`; assignment compatibility has one diagnostic owner, existing error types suppress derived mismatches, and destructuring-level errors dominate lower-level entry errors.

## Explicit Unit function bodies do not constrain ordinary tail-call results

## Extend specialization conflicts preserve instantiated target ownership

- problem type: duplicate-interface checks must distinguish disjoint instantiated extend targets and report a specialization conflict only when a generic target pattern can be consistently instantiated to the specialized target and its inherited interface becomes exactly equal.
- root cause: `CfirExtendTargetKey.ClassLike` correctly grouped declarations by nominal `ClassId` for provider candidate recall, but the rule query flattened every interface in that broad bucket and discarded its owner target pattern. `CfirExtendDuplicateInterfaceChecker` and `CfirExtendSpecializationConflictChecker` then treated the nominal bucket as conflict identity and used `semanticKey.contains("__EXT_TP_")` as a generic-pattern heuristic, producing false duplicates for disjoint tuple/function, nested `A`/`B`, inconsistent repeated-parameter, and distinct concrete instantiations.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 accepts `duplicate_impl_6.cj`, `duplicate_impl_6_1.cj`, `duplicate_impl_7.cj`, and `same_sign_default_in_multi_extend_impl01.cj` with no diagnostics. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExtend.cpp:183-267` builds the generic-target-to-specialized-target mapping, rejects inconsistent repeated bindings such as `T -> Int64` and `T -> String`, and reports `sema_extend_duplicate_interface` only when the substituted generic interface exactly equals the specialized interface. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/MultiTypeSubstUtils.cpp:342-361` recursively requires matching type kinds and declaration identity before producing a mapping.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/TypeExpansionUtils.kt`; `external/kotlin/core/compiler.common/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/types/AbstractStrictEqualityTypeChecker.kt`; `external/kotlin/core/compiler.common/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/types/AbstractTypeChecker.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/types/TypeUnification.kt`; and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/FirKotlinScopeProvider.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/cfir-common/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/session/services/CfirExtendRuleQueryService.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/services/CfirExtendSemanticModel.kt`; `CfirExtendIndexStore.kt`; `CfirExtendRuleQueryService.kt`; and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirExtendCheckers.kt`.
- repair principle: retain the nominal target key only as a broad candidate index, preserve complete instantiated target identity in the semantic model, and perform specialization comparison by structurally matching the generic target pattern before substituting and strictly comparing the inherited interface type.
- fixtures covered: PSI and non-PSI `duplicate_impl_1.cj`, `duplicate_impl_2.cj`, `duplicate_impl_3.cj`, `duplicate_impl_3_1.cj`, `duplicate_impl_4.cj`, `duplicate_impl_5.cj`, `duplicate_impl_5_1.cj`, `duplicate_impl_5_2.cj`, `duplicate_impl_5_3.cj`, `duplicate_impl_6.cj`, `duplicate_impl_6_1.cj`, `duplicate_impl_7.cj`, `duplicate_impl_builtin.cj`, `same_sign_default_in_multi_extend_impl01.cj`, `same_sign_default_in_multi_extend_impl02.cj`, and `generics_00038.cj`.
- fixture correction: none.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*SpecializationDuplicateCheckGenerated.testDuplicateImpl6' --tests '*SpecializationDuplicateCheckGenerated.testDuplicateImpl7' --tests '*SpecializationDuplicateCheckGenerated.testDuplicateImpl61' --tests '*GenericParamDeclCallInMemberFuncGenerated.testGenerics00038' --tests '*GenericParamDeclCallInMemberFuncGenerated.testSameSignDefaultInMultiExtendImpl01' --tests '*GenericParamDeclCallInMemberFuncGenerated.testSameSignDefaultInMultiExtendImpl02' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --quiet`.
- focused verification outcome: all false `EXTEND_DUPLICATE_INTERFACE` diagnostics disappeared. The six specialization negative methods passed on both PSI/LightTree paths; `generics_00038` and `same_sign_default_in_multi_extend_impl02` retained only their independent member-shadow/return-invariance differences.

## Function-body tail calls resolve before declared-return mismatch reporting

- problem type: a valid overloaded/generic call used as the final expression of a function with an incompatible explicit return type must resolve by its arguments first, then report the body mismatch on the complete tail expression.
- root cause: `CfirCheckExpectedReturnTypeBeforeArguments` rejected every concrete-`Unit` `std.core.print` overload against `main(): Int64` before argument checking; after that gate was opened, `CfirCallCompleter` still injected `Unit <: Int64` into the candidate constraint system and converted the valid generic call into `NEW_INFERENCE_ERROR`. The body checker also classified ordinary non-empty implicit tail-expression mismatches as `RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH`, although official Cangjie reports the expression-local mismatched-types diagnostic and reserves the body-level “because of return type” path for empty bodies.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports one `sema_mismatched_types` over the complete `print(a)`, expected `Int64` and found `Unit`; `external/cangjie_runtime/stdlib/libs/std/core/print.cj:80-83` defines `print<T>(arg: T, flush!: Bool = false): Unit where T <: ToString`; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeChecker.cpp:92-164`, `TypeCheckExpr/Block.cpp:43-92`, `TypeCheckCall.cpp:1395-1405`, `TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp:68-82`, `TypeCheckExpr/LoopExprs.cpp:36-44`, and `Diags.cpp:195-265` show that non-empty bodies target-check their real tail expression, while only an empty body is diagnosed at the function-body layer with the return-type “because” diagnostic.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/FirExplicitStarImportingScope.kt`; `FirAbstractStarImportingScope.kt`; `FirAbstractImportingScope.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/fir-deserialization/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/deserialization/AbstractFirDeserializedSymbolProvider.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/entrypoint/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/session/environment/MetadataSymbolProvider.kt`; and the existing CFIR expected-return refinement architecture derived from Kotlin FIR call-resolution stages.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirCheckExpectedReturnTypeBeforeArguments.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/CfirCallCompleter.kt`; `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirFunctionBodyTypeMismatchChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: keep declared-return expected types available for unresolved result variables and nested overload refinement, but never let a proper concrete tail-call result be rejected or made contradictory before the legal call is completed; diagnose non-empty implicit tails on the actual expression and use the body-level return mismatch only when no tail expression exists.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `call_error_report_01.cj` through `call_error_report_04.cj`; neighboring body-diagnostic guards `return/return1.cj`, `while-let-expr/while_let8.cj`, and `join_meet/join_05_2.cj`.
- fixture correction: official cjc proves the non-empty bare-reference and while-loop tails in `return1.cj` and `while_let8.cj` are ordinary `sema_mismatched_types`, so their inline names were corrected from `RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH` to `TYPE_MISMATCH`; the empty bodies in `join_05_2.cj` retain `RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH`.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.call.CallGenerated.testCallErrorReport03' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.call.CallGenerated.testCallErrorReport03' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --console=plain`.
- focused verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 4m 47s`; PSI and LightTree `testCallErrorReport03` both passed.
- family verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallErrorReport01' --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallErrorReport02' --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallErrorReport03' --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallErrorReport04' --tests '*ReturnGenerated.testReturn1' --tests '*WhileLetExprGenerated.testWhileLet8' --tests '*JoinMeetGenerated.testJoin052' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --console=plain`.

## Explicit-constructor completion diagnostics retain the declaration header

- problem type: `CLASS_UNINITIALIZED_FIELD` on an explicit constructor must underline the complete constructor declaration header from its modifiers through the parameter-list right parenthesis, not only the `init` keyword.
- root cause: commit `9b2b4d88f` changed the shared constructor-completeness report source in `CfirInitializationCheckers` from `constructorDeclarationHeaderDiagnosticSource()` back to `constructorNameDiagnosticSource()`. Both PSI and LightTree therefore pre-narrowed the source to the `init` token before the diagnostic factory positioning strategy ran, reverting an already verified range contract.
- official Cangjie evidence: this is a range-only problem governed by the repository Diagnostic Range Policy rather than `cjc`'s CLI anchor. Existing verified range entries at lines 1030-1058 require explicit and primary constructor completion diagnostics to cover the declaration header and exclude the body.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirMemberPropertiesChecker.kt`; `FirTopLevelPropertiesChecker.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/checkers-component-generator/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/checkers/generator/diagnostics/FirDiagnosticsList.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/frontend.common-psi/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/diagnostics/PositioningStrategies.kt`; and `LightTreePositioningStrategies.kt`. Kotlin models declaration-signature ranges symmetrically in PSI and LightTree, while Cangjie keeps its language-specific per-constructor completion diagnostic owner.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt` and `CfirDeclarationDiagnosticSources.kt`.
- repair principle: constructor-completion reporting stays in the shared initialization checker, but both source frontends must produce the exact constructor header or expose a violated source invariant; the checker must never degrade the diagnostic to the constructor name or whole declaration.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `class_init_constructor3.cj`, `class_init_constructor4.cj`, `class_init_constructor5.cj`, `class_init_with_nested_func0.cj`, and `class_init_with_nested_func1.cj`; guards include `static_or_global_var3.cj`, class/record `primaryConstructor2.cj`, and class/record `primaryConstructor8.cj`.

Historical fixtures also retained several incompatible whole-assignment and whole-left-value ranges for the same shared diagnostic owner.
- official Cangjie evidence: this is a range-only problem governed by the repository Diagnostic Range Policy. For a qualified assignment the relevant IDE token is the final selector; semantic firing and diagnostic-name multisets were unchanged in the triggering Class failures.

## Generic-instantiation member ambiguity retains inheritance provenance and reports once per trigger

- problem type: generic class/interface instantiation must preserve distinct inherited generic-interface member origins until concrete substitution, report `GENERIC_INSTANTIATION_CAUSES_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTIONS` once per actual instantiation trigger, and report instantiated duplicate supertypes on the complete type reference without diagnosing declaration supertype parameter forwarding.
- root cause: `CfirClassUseSiteMemberScope` flattened substituted inherited functions to their root declarations, losing the generic owner instance that distinguishes `I<X>.foo` from `I<Y>.foo`; after provenance was restored, the file checker still keyed reports by source plus function name, so one `II<Int32>` trigger produced separate `foo` and `fs` diagnostics. The trigger collector also lacked a structural boundary between `class B<X,Y> <: A<X,Y>` forwarding and actual concrete/repeated instantiation, while duplicate-supertype reporting narrowed the retained type-ref source to the classifier token.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports exactly four ambiguity diagnostics in `interface_default_implemented_func_invalid_6.cj` (`B<X,X>`, inferred `B`, inferred `test`, and explicit `test<Int64>`) and none on `class B<X,Y> <: A<X,Y>`. For `interface_generic11.cj`, cjc reports exactly six ambiguity diagnostics, one on each concrete `II<...>` supertype reference, even though every reference produces both instance `foo` and static `fs` conflicts; additional probes with multiple conflicting names likewise retain one diagnostic per trigger source. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/InstantiatedChecker.cpp:56-119,412-433` keeps member signatures distinct but anchors the top-level diagnostic at the instantiation trigger; `include/cangjie/Basic/DiagnosticEngine.h:540-570` deduplicates diagnostics by source range and severity; `src/Sema/TypeChecker.cpp:2545-2565,2597-2697` separates declaration duplicate-interface checks from concrete type/expression instantiation checks.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/FirTypeIntersectionScopeContext.kt`; `AbstractFirUseSiteMemberScope.kt`; `FirClassSubstitutionScope.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirImplementationMismatchChecker.kt`; `FirSupertypesChecker.kt`; and `external/kotlin/compiler/frontend.common/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/diagnostics/impl/DeduplicatingDiagnosticReporter.kt`. Kotlin retains overridden members with their base scopes in provider layers and deduplicates declaration diagnostics by source plus factory at the checker/reporter boundary.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/scopes/impl/CfirClassUseSiteMemberScope.kt`; `CfirClassSubstitutionScope.kt`; and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirGenericInstantiationChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: provider scopes retain complete direct-input/root member, generic owner instance, substitution, and base-scope provenance; the checker structurally suppresses only one-to-one declaration-supertype parameter forwarding, checks concrete/repeated/mixed instantiations, and deduplicates this diagnostic by trigger source rather than deleting any callable member.

Instantiated `SUPER_TYPES_DUPLICATE` ranges now cover the complete `II<...>` type reference according to the Diagnostic Range Policy.

## Nested callable capture of uninitialized instance storage

- problem type: a nested named function or lambda inside an instance constructor that assigns an uninitialized instance field must report `CAPTURE_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION`, must not initialize the outer constructor state, and must leave constructor completion reporting intact.
- root cause: `CfirInitializationFlowAnalyzer` already traversed nested callable bodies in an isolated state and discarded their assignment effects, but `InitializationState.shouldReportCaptureBeforeInitialization` classified only `LOCAL_VARIABLE`; constructor-tracked fields are `INSTANCE_MEMBER`, so their nested writes skipped the capture diagnostic while correctly remaining uninitialized at constructor exit.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports exactly `CAPTURE_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION(a)` plus `CLASS_UNINITIALIZED_FIELD(a)` for `class_init_with_nested_func0.cj` and `_1.cj`, and no initialization error for `_2.cj`. `variable_use_before_init_07.cj` proves local `var`/`let` nested writes report capture while outer reads remain used-before, whereas static storage does not report capture and remains statically uninitialized. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/InitializationChecker.cpp:190-212,752-813,862-895,1481-1521,1600-1656` classifies cross-callable capture, explicitly prevents captured assignments from updating initialization state, preserves illegal-member priority for nested reads, excludes global/static storage, and reports constructor completion.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/dfa/cfg/ControlFlowGraphBuilder.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/semantics/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/dfa/cfg/CFGNode.kt`; `ControlFlowGraph.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/cfa/VariableInitializationCheckProcessor.kt`; `FirPropertyInitializationAnalyzer.kt`; and `util/PropertyInitializationInfoCollector.kt`. Kotlin separates local/anonymous callable subgraphs from outer initialization flow and treats callable-scope crossing independently from storage-kind diagnostic classification.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`.
- repair principle: make capture eligibility an explicit tracked-storage property (`LOCAL_VARIABLE` and `INSTANCE_MEMBER`, excluding `STATIC_OR_GLOBAL`) while preserving member-initializer illegal-access priority, nested-state discard, callee-effect isolation, and return-target identity.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `class_init_with_nested_func0/1/2.cj`; `InitializationCheck/capture_func_rules_local_0101.cj` and `variable_use_before_init_07.cj`; `function_capture1/2/3.cj`; `lambda_capture/capture_not_init_01/02.cj`; `lambda_spawn.cj`; and `super_this_12.cj` as the independent open/abstract `this`-capture boundary.
- fixture correction: cjc reports three `CAPTURE_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION` diagnostics in `capture_not_init_02.cj` (assignment, do-while condition, and return) because the captured assignment does not advance nested state; the fixture was corrected to include the two missing later references without changing source grammar.
- family verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassInitWithNestedFunc0' --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassInitWithNestedFunc1' --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassInitWithNestedFunc2' --tests '*InitializationCheckGenerated.testVariableUseBeforeInit07' --tests '*InitializationCheckGenerated.testCaptureFuncRulesLocal0101' --tests '*FunctionGenerated.testFunctionCapture1' --tests '*FunctionGenerated.testFunctionCapture2' --tests '*FunctionGenerated.testFunctionCapture3' --tests '*LambdaCaptureGenerated.testCaptureNotInit01' --tests '*LambdaCaptureGenerated.testCaptureNotInit02' --tests '*LambdaGenerated.testLambdaSpawn' --tests '*SuperThisGenerated.testSuperThis12' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-configuration-cache --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --no-build-cache`.

## Callable override type parameters are compared by alpha-equivalence

- problem type: parent and child generic functions that override/redefine each other must compare corresponding callable type parameters in one shared type-parameter space after owner substitution; distinct symbols created for the parent use-site copy must not manufacture return-type conflicts.
- root cause: `CfirClassSubstitutionScope` correctly rebuilt the inherited function copy and its callable type parameters, and `CfirOverrideChecker` already mapped the parent callable parameters to the child by position. `CfirInheritanceDeepChecker.functionReturnTypeConflict`, however, compared the parent copy return type and child return type directly, so `V_parent_copy` and `V_child` were treated as unrelated symbols and produced false `RETURN_TYPE_INCOMPATIBLE` / `RETURN_TYPE_INVARIANCE` diagnostics.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports only the call-site generic constraint mismatch, the two illegal primitive upper bounds, and `GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_NOT_LOOSER` for `class_redef_11.cj`; it reports no return-type diagnostic. It accepts `class_redef_12.cj` with zero diagnostics. Thus corresponding parent/child callable type parameters are alpha-equivalent for return comparison even after the parent owner type has been instantiated.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/FirClassSubstitutionScope.kt`; `FirStandardOverrideChecker.kt`; `FirAbstractOverrideChecker.kt` (`buildSubstitutorForOverridesCheck`); `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/FirOverrideChecker.kt`; and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirOverrideChecker.kt`.

- repair principle: construct one providers-layer parent-current-copy to child callable type-parameter substitutor, require equal arity, and make every override return/constraint comparison consume it before invariance or subtype checks; never truncate the mapping or compare un-substituted fallback types.

## Declaration-tailed function bodies preserve Unit semantics and declaration ownership

- problem type: an explicitly non-Unit function whose body ends in a declaration must treat the declaration as producing `Unit`, report the mismatch on that declaration, and remain distinct from a genuinely empty body.
- root cause: `CfirFunctionBodyTypeMismatchChecker` converted the final statement directly to `CfirExpression`. A declaration tail therefore became `null`, which correctly implied `Unit` but incorrectly lost the declaration source and made the checker classify the body as empty, producing `RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH` over the whole block instead of `TYPE_MISMATCH` over the final declaration.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_mismatched_types` on the complete `var value: Data = Data()` declaration in `class3.cj`, with `expected 'Int64', found 'Unit'` and the note `definitions and declarations are always of type 'Unit'`. A minimized empty body instead reports `sema_mismatched_types_because` over the body. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/Block.cpp:21-40,70-80` gives declaration tails the `Unit` type and diagnoses the final declaration; `TypeChecker.cpp:134-144` reserves the body-level path for an empty body; `Diags.cpp:195-207,248-264` owns the two diagnostic forms.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/BodyResolveUtils.kt:122-131`; `FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt:852-868`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirFunctionReturnChecker.kt:37-43`; `FirErrors.kt:1021`; `PositioningStrategies.kt:663-669`; and `LightTreePositioningStrategies.kt:1214-1228`. Kotlin likewise separates the block result expression from the syntactic final statement/source.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirFunctionBodyTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; fixture correction in `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/class/class3.cj`.
- repair principle: model `tailStatement`, `tailExpression`, `actualType`, and `resultSource` separately so declaration tails remain semantically `Unit` while preserving their own diagnostic ownership; only `statements.isEmpty()` may use the empty-body source and diagnostic path.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `class3.cj`; `class/static_call_non_static/class_static_call_non_static1.cj`; `record/static_call_non_static/record_static_call_non_static1.cj`; `join_meet/join_05_2.cj`; and the getter-empty-body portion of `enum/enum17_prop2.cj`.

## Bare static qualifier function references form overload ambiguity before visibility filtering

- problem type: a type-name-qualified, standalone static function value with no expected type must form its overload set before accessibility filtering, so an inaccessible private static overload still participates in `AMBIGUOUS_USE`; ordinary calls, typed function references, and object-receiver values retain their distinct visibility order.
- root cause: `CfirCandidateCollector` retained both static overload discoveries from the same best tower group, but `CfirCallResolver.reduceCandidates` applied `candidate.isSuccessful` to every standalone function value before preserving the overload set. Outside the declaring class, the private overload therefore disappeared before ambiguity construction, while the same source inside the class kept both candidates and behaved correctly.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_ambiguous_use` for both the in-class and out-of-class `Test1.foo` expressions in `class_access_control17.cj`, listing the public `foo()` and private `foo(Int64)` candidates. A typed out-of-class `(Int64) -> Int64 = Test1.foo` instead selects the private overload and reports `sema_invalid_access_function`, while `Test1.foo(1)` follows ordinary call resolution and excludes the private overload before argument checking. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp:634-681`, `TypeCheckReference.cpp:376-394,449-495`, `TypeCheckAccess.cpp:93-126`, and `Diags.cpp:452-470` separate static target discovery, bare-reference ambiguity, later access checking, and ambiguity reporting.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/candidate/CallKind.kt`; `stages/ResolutionStages.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/semantics/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/ResolutionDiagnostic.kt`; `candidate/CandidateCollector.kt`; and `FirCallResolver.kt`. Kotlin remains visibility/applicability-first, so it supplies only the candidate-discovery and diagnostic-layer architecture; the pre-visibility bare-static rule is Cangjie-specific and comes solely from official Cangjie evidence.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt`.
- repair principle: in the shared function-value candidate-selection policy, preserve the collector's same-best-group, pre-visibility overload set only for standalone `NamedValueAccess` with no expected type, no explicit type arguments, a real qualifier scope, and more than one genuinely static `CfirFunction`; typed references are handled separately by expected-type target selection, while ordinary calls, no-expected-type object receivers, and explicit-type-argument paths continue to use their accessibility-first rules.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `class_access_control15.cj`, `class_access_control16.cj`, `class_access_control17.cj`, `class_access_control18.cj`, `overload/overload_resolution_1.cj`, and `call/call_reference_inference_01/02/03.cj`.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassAccessControl15' --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassAccessControl16' --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassAccessControl17' --tests '*ClassGenerated.testClassAccessControl18' --tests '*OverloadGenerated.testOverloadResolution1' --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallReferenceInference01' --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallReferenceInference02' --tests '*CallGenerated.testCallReferenceInference03' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache`.
- verification outcome: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 8m 24s`; XML reported 16 tests across six PSI/LightTree generated suites with 0 failures and 0 errors.

## Typed function references select by signature before reporting target legality

- problem type: a standalone function value with an expected function type must select declarations by callable signature before reporting accessibility or other candidate-local legality errors; a uniquely matching private declaration reports `INVISIBLE_MEMBER`, while only a genuine absence of signature-compatible declarations reports `NO_MATCH_FUNCTION_DECLARATION_FOR_REF`.
- root cause: `CfirCallResolver.reduceCandidates` filtered every typed standalone function value through `candidate.isSuccessful`, dropping inaccessible discoveries before expected-type selection. Its isolated `completedFunctionReferenceType` probe also rejected any unsuccessful candidate, so a signature-compatible private target was reclassified as a type mismatch and `ConeNoMatchingFunctionReferenceError` shadowed the existing visibility diagnostic path.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 selects private static `A.f()` for `let f: () -> Int64 = A.f` and then reports `sema_invalid_access_function`; `(Int64) -> Int64 = A.f` selects the accessible overload and succeeds. The same expected-type-before-access order holds for object receiver function values, whereas no-expected-type object values and ordinary calls filter inaccessible declarations first. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp:327-388,634-681`, `TypeCheckReference.cpp:635-665`, `TypeCheckAccess.cpp:93-126`, and `TypeCheckCall.cpp:1824-1859,2260-2308` own those separate selection and legality orders.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/candidate/CallKind.kt`; `stages/ResolutionStages.kt`; `stages/CheckCallableReferenceExpectedType.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/semantics/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/ResolutionDiagnostic.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/resolution.common/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/resolve/calls/tower/CandidateApplicability.kt`; `candidate/CandidateCollector.kt`; `FirCallResolver.kt`; and `ResolveUtils.kt`. Kotlin keeps expected-type compatibility and candidate legality as distinct stages and preserves the selected candidate's own error.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt`; official-evidence guard added to `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/class/class_static04.cj`.
- repair principle: typed function-reference compatibility is determined only by parameter shape, resulting callable type, constraint consistency, completion, and final function-type subtyping; candidate-local diagnostics never mean signature mismatch and remain attached to the selected original candidate for the normal diagnostic mapper.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `class_static04.cj` for both static and object private targets; `func_assign_var.cj`, `constraint_check/expose6.cj`, and `Extend/extend_subtype3.cj` as genuine no-match guards; `overloaded_func_01.cj` and `overload_resolution_1.cj` as successful expected-type overload selection; `function_access.cj` as ordinary-call visibility; `class_access_control15/16/17/18.cj` and `call_reference_inference_01/02/03.cj` as no-expected-type visibility and ambiguity guards.

## Illegal-position `super()` preserves its nominal receiver type

- problem type: a resolved `super(...)` call outside the constructor-header position must report its independent placement error while retaining the constructed superclass type for following member access; a missing member reports `NOT_MEMBER_OF`, and an existing member resolves without an unresolved-reference cascade.
- root cause: `CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.transformConstructorDelegationCall` assigned `Unit` to every successfully resolved `this(...)` / `super(...)` call. That is correct only for the declaration-level constructor-header delegation. A non-header `super()` therefore lost its nominal receiver and made `super().a`, `super().c`, and `super().c++` resolve against `Unit` or an error receiver.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc 1.0.5` reports `sema_illegal_place_of_calling_this_or_super` plus `sema_not_member_of` for `super().a`, but only the placement diagnostic for `super().c` and `super().c++`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeChecker.cpp:1336-1367` checks constructor-call placement independently, and `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp:295-325` reports missing members only after confirming that the base expression has a correct nominal type.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, `FirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`, and the generated `FirDelegatedConstructorCall` model; Kotlin keeps the constructed type reference and completed constructor candidate on the call node instead of replacing the resolved receiver model with an unrelated fallback type.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`.
- repair principle: constructor-call resolution always preserves the selected constructed type, while only the constructor-header expression surface is projected to `Unit`; placement legality remains a declaration-checker concern and never destroys receiver typing.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `class/invalid_super_call.cj`; guards include `record/record_this.cj`, `class/super_this/recursive_constructor_call.cj`, class and record `constructor/primaryConstructor/primaryConstructor8.cj`, and the complete PSI/LightTree `ClassGenerated` suites.

## Record selective dependency topology and declaration-owned metadata lookup

## Ordinary assignment RHS expected-type mismatch ownership

- problem type: ordinary `lValue = rValue` must classify and report the RHS expected-type failure at the assignment owner without reusing the VArray-only `ASSIGNMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH`, duplicating literal overflow, or losing the pre-error actual type of calls and composite expressions.
- root cause: the assignment checker recomputed mismatch semantics from the final RHS tree and receiver syntax after body resolve had already replaced some call/array roots with `ConeErrorType`. That erased the actual type, made ordinary assignments depend on expression shape, emitted `ASSIGNMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` outside the VArray path, and allowed `LITERAL_NUMERIC_OVERFLOW` or `TYPE_INCOMPATIBLE` cascades that the official assignment check does not produce.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/AssignExpr.cpp:329-398` performs the ordinary RHS `Check` and keeps VArray/subscript handling separate; `TypeCheckUtil.cpp:228-231` owns the generic mismatch; `TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp:68-82` preserves name-reference typing; `TypeCheckExpr/LitConstExpr.cpp:26-125,182-190` distinguishes `boolean`, `integer`, `floating-point`, and `character` conversion failures. `cjc 1.0.5` confirms that ordinary assignments use `sema_mismatched_types`, direct incompatible Bool/Int/Float/Rune literals use only `sema_cannot_convert_literal`, Unit uses only the mismatch, direct String additionally keeps the assignment-level incompatibility, and VArray subscript assignment remains a separate contract.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt:1424-1474`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/BodyResolveContext.kt:93-106`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/expression/FirAssignmentTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`. Kotlin supplies the assignment-RHS expected-type frame and checker separation; Cangjie-specific diagnostic selection remains governed by the official compiler.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/cfir-tree/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/expressions/CfirAssignmentTypeMismatchOutcome.kt`; `cfir/cfir-tree/tree-generator/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/tree/generator/CfirTree.kt`; `Types.kt`; generated `CfirAssignment.kt`, `CfirAssignmentBuilder.kt`, and `CfirAssignmentImpl.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/BodyResolveContext.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/CfirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`; `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirAssignmentTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; `CfirLiteralNumericOverflowChecker.kt`; and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/CfirTypeSemanticsDiagnostics.kt`.

## Enum pattern target typing and local lambda initializer PCLA boundaries

## Invalid expression recovery through operators, member calls, and string interpolation

- problem type: invalid root expressions must propagate a non-reporting error type through later operator calls, member access, member-call arguments, and string interpolation instead of producing secondary `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH_PRIMITIVE_EXTEND`, `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`, `NOT_MEMBER_OF`, `INVALID_UNARY_EXPR`, `INVALID_BINARY_OPERATOR`, or invoke diagnostics.
- root cause: CFIR already had `ConeUnreportedDuplicateDiagnostic` but used it only on selected paths. Logical `&&` / `||` were typed as `Bool` even when operand types were invalid, primitive-operator fast resolution ignored `ConeErrorType` operands, member lookup only treated recoverable nominal receiver diagnostics as dominating, call argument resolution still descended into arguments after an explicit receiver had become an error, and string interpolation always wrote `String` even when a part expression was already invalid.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc 1.0.5 --diagnostic-format=noColor` on `codex-probes/errmsgs_binary_recovery.cj` reports only the two root invalid `+` diagnostics; `codex-probes/errmsgs_composition_recovery.cj` reports only the root invalid `&&`; `codex-probes/errmsgs_error_value_cascade.cj` reports only the root invalid `+` before later member/unary/binary/invoke uses; `codex-probes/errmsgs_error_callee_arguments.cj` reports the root invalid `+` and the independent generic-argument error, but no `e3` unresolved cascade; `codex-probes/errmsgs_error_callee_argument_root.cj` reports only the receiver root error. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/BinaryExpr.cpp:706-840` owns logical/binary operator synthesis and root diagnostics; `TypeCheckExpr/UnaryExpr.cpp:55-95` reports a unary error only when the operand synthesizes a correct type; `TypeCheckCall.cpp:2618-2623` suppresses call diagnostics when invalid argument types were already reported; `TypeCheckExpr/LitConstExpr.cpp:146-175` makes the whole interpolation invalid when any interpolated expression check fails.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt` for boolean operators and string concatenation traversal, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/diagnostics/coneDiagnosticToFirDiagnostic.kt:405-458` for suppressing ambiguity diagnostics when call operands already contain error types.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`, `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt`, and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`.
- repair principle: once a subexpression owns the root semantic error, later expressions keep type-shape information only as delegated type metadata and otherwise propagate a `ConeUnreportedDuplicateDiagnostic`; diagnostics are suppressed only for the same operator/member/call cascade whose operand or receiver already carries an error type.

## Argument-mapping failures terminate call checking and propagate InvalidTy through outer calls

- problem type: ordinary arity and named-argument mapping failures must own one primary call diagnostic, terminate argument/lambda checking for that candidate, and remain semantically invalid through enclosing calls so later member access does not report a derived error.
- root cause: `ArgumentMappingOutcome` recorded mapping failures but argument checking and completion did not consume that state. Error candidates either stopped before the completion writer could finalize nested lambdas or continued with partial mappings, producing argument/lambda cascades. After the immediate failed call became `ConeErrorType`, successful enclosing calls still wrote their normal declaration result types, so `Config(...)` invalidity was lost through `Option.Some(...)` and `App(...)` and the later `.run()` was incorrectly diagnosed as `NOT_MEMBER_OF`.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports only `sema_wrong_number_of_arguments` for `trailing_closure03.cj`, `trailing_closure06.cj`, and `trailing_closure16.cj`, and only `sema_multiple_named_argument` for `trailing_closure_named_args_02.cj`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:50-74,618-672,1365-1408` terminates candidate checking after ordinary arity or named mapping failure; `TypeCheckCall.cpp:2227-2232` returns `InvalidTy` for a failed call; `TypeCheckCall.cpp:2611-2623` suppresses derived call diagnostics when an argument is already invalid. For `enum6_test.cj`, cjc reports the three independent undeclared-type errors plus only `sema_need_named_argument` at `16:44-81`; an equivalent `Option<Int64>` probe still reports only `sema_need_named_argument`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp:291-309` does not report a missing member when the base expression has invalid type.

## Trailing lambda on a non-function formal reports its dedicated mapping diagnostic

- problem type: a trailing lambda mapped to `Any` or to a generic formal without a function upper bound must report `TRAILING_LAMBDA_CANNOT_USED_FOR_NON_FUNCTION` on the complete lambda instead of degrading to `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`, an argument mismatch, or an invalid source range.

## Trailing-lambda legality is owned by mapped formals, not dispatch receivers

- problem type: a legal trailing lambda on a member function whose last formal is a function type must not be rejected because the member call's dispatch receiver is a non-function class instance.

It inspected `CfirFunctionCall.explicitReceiver`; for `Select<Unit>().otherwise { ... }` that receiver is `Select<Unit>`, not the `() -> Unit` formal, so the checker reported `TRAILING_LAMBDA_CANNOT_USED_FOR_NON_FUNCTION` over the entire otherwise call.

- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/FirArgumentsToParametersMapper.kt:69-112,249-278`, which maps an external lambda to the final formal and does not add a post-resolution dispatch-receiver check.

- repair principle: keep trailing-lambda target legality in the shared argument-to-parameter mapper, where the actual mapped formal is available, and remove the contradictory post-resolution checker registration instead of trying to infer a formal type from receiver syntax.

## Callable-value trailing lambdas are ordinary positional arguments

- problem type: a trailing lambda passed while invoking a callable value must be mapped to the callable value's final parameter and checked as an ordinary value argument; when that parameter is non-functional, the result is `TYPE_MISMATCH` for the complete lambda, not a declaration-call trailing-lambda diagnostic or an invoke-resolution failure.
- root cause: callable-value identity was inferred independently in arity, variadic, ordinary-argument, and trailing-lambda mapping paths. Direct variables and synthetic function-type `invoke` candidates therefore entered different mappings. After mapping was unified, a lambda against a non-function expected type still wrote `(P...) -> fresh R <: Expected` before its body fixed `R`; the constraint appeared compatible initially and later degraded into a contradiction without structured `ArgumentTypeMismatch`.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports exactly two `sema_mismatched_types` diagnostics on the two complete `{}` expressions in `trailing_closure13.cj`, each with expected `Int64` and actual `() -> Unit`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:2147-2224` creates positional parameters from `FuncTy.paramTys` for callable-value invocation, and `LambdaExpr.cpp:321-330` synthesizes the lambda's own function type before ordinary mismatch checking when the target is not functional.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt:423-561`; `FirCallCompleter.kt:69-127`; and the FIR candidate/call-kind structure. Kotlin keeps callable identity on the candidate and postpones lambda-body completion while preserving a structured argument mismatch.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/candidate/Candidate.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/CangjieVariadicUtils.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/CfirMapArguments.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/stages/ArgumentCheckingProcessor.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/inference/PostponedArgumentsAnalyzer.kt`; and `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`.
- repair principle: make callable-value identity a candidate invariant consumed by every mapping decision, then check a non-target-typed lambda only after its body has produced the final intrinsic function type; declaration-call syntax rules never replace ordinary callable-value argument typing.

## LightTree call flattening preserves source ownership

- problem type: LightTree construction of a call with a trailing lambda must never assign a call source whose end precedes its start; a parser-generated inner `CALL_EXPRESSION` owns the call suffix only when it directly contains a value-argument or type-argument list.
- root cause: `LightTreeRawCfirExpressionBuilder.convertCall` conflated callee unwrapping, argument inheritance, and source ownership. For simple `x {}`, a degenerate inner call with no suffix became the effective source owner and was then trimmed using the outer lambda offset, producing the invalid range `(50, 48)`.
- official Cangjie evidence: this is a range-only structural defect governed by the repository Diagnostic Range Policy. The complete `{}` is the relevant token range for the official mismatch; no diagnostic layer may clamp a malformed CFIR source.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/raw-fir/light-tree2fir/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/lightTree/LightTreeRawFirExpressionBuilder.kt:741-850`, where each real call suffix owns its source and no degenerate nested call is promoted merely because a trailing lambda exists.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/raw-cfir/light-tree2cfir/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/lightTree/LightTreeRawCfirExpressionBuilder.kt`.
- repair principle: separate callee unwrapping from call-suffix/source ownership; only a nested node with a real value/type argument list may be flattened as the source owner, and trimming asserts that the trailing lambda lies inside that owner.
- fixtures covered: LightTree and PSI `trailing_closure13.cj`; source guards `trailing_closure01/02/03/06/07/09.cj`, `trailing_closure_nesting_01.cj`, and `trailing_closure_type_mismatch_01/_02.cj`; the complete `TrailingClosureGenerated` suites.

## Generic override constraints aggregate parent contracts and preserve transitive generic bounds

- problem type: generic override/redef members must compare each child type-parameter constraint once against the complete inherited contract: bounds inside one declaration form an intersection, while equivalent members inherited from different parents contribute a union of parent domains.
- root cause: `CfirOverrideChecker.checkGenericConstraintCompatibility` iterated parents independently and flattened each declaration's bounds into unrelated entries. That made a single `A & B` parent constraint look stricter than its effective intersection, lost multi-parent aggregation, and lacked the generic-bound transitive closure required for `T1 <: T2 <: T3 <: T4`. An intermediate repair incorrectly removed illegal upper bounds from the comparison; official Cangjie reports their legality error but deliberately retains them in the override constraint graph.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports D/E and accepts F in `generic_constraint_inheritance_02/03`, reports only D in `_07`, retains `GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_NOT_LOOSER` in `generic_upper_constraint_inheritance_01/03`, and reports no such diagnostic in `generic_upper_constraint_inheritance_04/05`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/MergeInheritedMemberHelper.cpp:29-63,135-180,213-227` maps and unions same-signature parent bounds; `StructInheritanceChecker.cpp:234-270,1214-1267` retains generic bounds, constructs a per-declaration intersection, and applies the two-part looser comparison; `PreCheck.cpp:1035-1060,1100-1130` diagnoses illegal bounds without deleting them.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/FirTypeIntersectionScopeContext.kt:209-240,337-365`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/tree/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/symbols/impl/FirFunctionSymbol.kt:66-81`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirOverrideChecker.kt:367-375`. Kotlin supplies the complete direct-override/intersection-symbol data flow; Cangjie semantics come from the official compiler.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirOverrideChecker.kt`; fixture corrections in `generic_constraint_inheritance_02.cj`, `_03.cj`, `_07.cj`, `generic_upper_constraint_inheritance_04.cj`, and `_05.cj`.
- repair principle: build one cycle-safe direct-and-transitive effective intersection per declaration, substitute every parent into the child callable domain, retain the cross-parent union, and run the official two-part comparison once per child type parameter.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `generic_constraint_inheritance_01.cj` through `_08.cj` and `generic_upper_constraint_inheritance_01.cj` through `_11.cj`; the focused semantic fixtures are `_02`, `_03`, `_07`, `generic_upper_01`, `_03`, `_04`, and `_05`.
- fixture correction: `_02/_03` now expect the cjc-proven D/E diagnostics and accept F; `_07` uses the complete constraint diagnostic owner; `generic_upper_04/_05` retain only the official upper-bound legality diagnostics on complete type-parameter tokens.
