## Generic upper-bound member conflicts use use-site members and official diagnostic precedence

- problem type: generic upper-bound intersections must include visible extend members, choose the most specific class bound, report incompatible inherited member types on the complete constraint, and suppress a weaker visibility diagnostic when the same implicit implementation already has an incompatible return type.
- root cause: `CfirTypeParameterBoundsChecker` correctly selected the most specific class bound but created a `DECLARATION_SITE` member scope, which intentionally excludes extend members; `_09/_10` therefore never saw `extend C/B.foo`. Separately, `CfirInheritanceDeepChecker` computed a return-type conflict and then independently emitted `CANNOT_WEAKEN_ACCESS_PRIVILEGE` for the same implicit `S.foo`/`I2.foo` relation.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports exactly two upper-bound legality errors plus `sema_return_type_incompatible` for `generic_upper_constraint_inheritance_06`, without weak visibility; when the return type is made compatible it reports weak visibility instead. It reports exactly one `sema_inherit_member_type_inconsistent` on the complete constraint in `_09/_10` and no `x.foo()` cascade. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/StructInheritanceChecker.cpp:1174-1201,1353-1407` establishes return/visibility precedence; `GenericInheritanceChecker.cpp:23-95`, `StructInheritanceChecker.cpp:447-471`, and `PreCheck.cpp:928-951` select the smallest class and merge its visible extend members with interface members.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirOverrideChecker.kt:436-466`; `FirImplementationMismatchChecker.kt:80-120`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/scopes/ScopeUtils.kt:100-121`; and FIR type-intersection scope/context implementations. Kotlin supplies checker ownership and use-site intersection scope structure only.

## Hide compile-time visibility is parser-owned annotation metadata

- problem type: ordinary `@Hide` is compile-time invisible and must report `HIDE_COMPILE_TIME_INVISIBLE`, while `@!Hide` is compile-time visible; ordinary function parameters report `HIDE_AT_FUNC_PARAM` first and do not continue into Hide visibility or argument checks.
- root cause: CFIR discarded the parser-owned `@`/`@!` semantic bit and later guessed visibility from annotation type resolution, so a successfully resolved ordinary `@Hide` looked visible. Macro-expression construction could also replace the annotation source with its input declaration range, preventing the checker from owning the complete annotation token precisely.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Parse/ParseAnnotations.cpp:236-257` sets `Annotation::isCompileTimeVisible` only for `AT_EXCL`; `external/cangjie_compiler/include/cangjie/AST/Node.h:567-593` stores that bit on the annotation node; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Plugin/PluginCustomAnnoChecker.cpp:478-496` gives ordinary function parameters `sema_hide_at_func_param` precedence with `continue`, otherwise reports `sema_hide_compile_time_invisible` on the complete annotation when the bit is false. `ASTWriter.cpp:1642-1735` and `ASTLoader.cpp:630-666` preserve compile-time-visible annotations across module serialization.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/tree/gen/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/expressions/FirAnnotationCall.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/tree/gen/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/expressions/impl/FirAnnotationCallImpl.kt`. FIR keeps source and resolution metadata on the annotation call itself; CFIR's stable equivalent across macro splice is the session annotation-slot snapshot and registry.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/providers/macro/CfirAnnotationMetadataRegistry.kt`; `cfir/raw-cfir/psi2cfir/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/builder/PsiRawCfirBuilder.kt`; `cfir/raw-cfir/light-tree2cfir/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/lightTree/LightTreeRawCfirDeclarationBuilder.kt`; `compiler/frontend/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/frontend/pipeline/MacroExpandPhase.kt`; `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirBuiltInAnnotationSemanticsChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: capture compile-time visibility and the complete annotation source once at every raw-builder annotation slot, preserve both through macro cache/splice identity migration, and make semantic checkers consume that metadata instead of re-deriving it from resolved types or source text.

## Recursive constructor graph ignores unresolved error constructor candidates

- problem type: an arity-invalid `this()`/`super()` constructor call must still report its call/placement diagnostic, but it must not create a semantic dependency edge for `RECURSIVE_CONSTRUCTOR_CALL`.
- root cause: `CfirResolvedErrorReference` implements `CfirResolvedNamedReference` and preserves the best candidate symbol for later diagnostics. `CfirRecursiveConstructorCallChecker` treated every resolved named reference as an applicable constructor target, so `invalid_init_call_1.cj` incorrectly turned an arity-invalid `this()` into a real recursive-constructor edge.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Utils.cpp:42-45` defines init references from `node.GetTarget()` and `IsInstanceConstructor`; `Utils.cpp:116-168,543-555` builds the recursive constructor graph only from constructor declarations and those concrete init references. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:2548,2948-2976` treats `this()` as a normal declared function call and only reaches post-check/target writeback after a successful call match.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirCommonConstructorDelegationIssuesChecker.kt:89-107`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/tree/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/references/FirReferenceUtils.kt:30-35,70-71`. Kotlin's constructor-delegation checker asks for `toResolvedConstructorSymbol(discardErrorReference = true)`, so error references are not constructor-chain edges.

## Target-typed composite expression result checks use the real tail owner

- problem type: explicit target types on variable initializers, field initializers, default parameter values, assignments, `return expr`, function-body tails, `match`, and normal `try` must be checked against the real result expression inside `block`/two-branch `if`/`match`/`try`, instead of comparing the composite root's joined type and reporting `TYPE_MISMATCH` on the whole root.
- root cause: initializer, return, body-tail, and assignment checkers compared the composite expression root after resolve; `CfirMatchTargetTypeMismatchChecker` and `CfirTryTargetTypeMismatchChecker` had their own partial branch walkers; `CfirTargetTypedTailExpressionUtils` existed but was not the shared owner. This let `if6.cj` infer a composite root type and emit a root mismatch rather than checking the mismatching branch expression.
- official Cangjie evidence: `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckDecl.cpp` calls `Check(ctx, vd.type->ty, vd.initializer.get())` for explicitly typed variable initializers; `TypeCheckExpr/IfExpr.cpp` routes two-branch if expressions through `ChkIfExprTwoBranches` and checks both branches against the target, while `ChkIfExprNoElse` fixes no-final-else if expressions to `Unit`; `TypeCheckExpr/Block.cpp` checks only the last block node and treats tail declarations as `Unit`; `TypeCheckExpr/TryExpr.cpp` checks normal try/catch/handler bodies against the target and keeps try-with-resources as `Unit`. A local cjc 1.0.5 probe for `let b: A = if (false) { let c = 1 } else { A() }` reports `sema_mismatched_types` on the complete `let c = 1`, expected `Class-A`, found `Unit`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirControlFlowStatementsResolveTransformer.kt`; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/inference/FirCallCompletionResultsWriterTransformer.kt`. Kotlin uses synthetic call expected types and completion writeback so `when`/`try` branch results receive target typing rather than leaving only a root mismatch.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirTargetTypedTailExpressionUtils.kt`; initializer mismatch checkers for fields, pattern variables, and value parameters; `CfirReturnTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; `CfirFunctionBodyTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; `CfirAssignmentTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; `CfirMatchTargetTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; `CfirTryTargetTypeMismatchChecker.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirExpressionsResolveTransformer.kt`.
- repair principle: make one checker utility own target-typed composite result descent, then let every target context consume its `Handled/NotHandled` outcome before falling back to the caller's existing root-level diagnostic category.

## Interface static default implementation calls require complete static dependencies

- problem type: nominal static calls must report `INTERFACE_CALL_WITH_UNIMPLEMENTED_CALL` when they directly access an abstract static member or when a concrete interface static default implementation recursively uses a static interface function/property that the final qualifier interface type does not concretely implement.

A call such as `I2.f2()` could resolve to a concrete default body even though that body called an unimplemented `f1`, so the expression checker never saw the official call-site error. ## Static members cannot depend on owner generic parameters

- problem type: static fields, properties, and static initializers of a generic class-like or extend declaration must report `STATIC_VARIABLE_USE_GENERIC_PARAMETER` on every dependent type/reference/expression; failed static exposed-member access such as `T.m2` must preserve the same repository diagnostic without emitting upper-bound member-lookup cascades.
- root cause: the declaration checker did not share one traversal across class-like and extend owners, omitted static initializer bodies and explicit receiver types, and did not record root diagnostic ranges for cascade suppression. ## Static/global initialization follows property accessors and field-level static-init roots

- problem type: global/static initialization dependency analysis must enter the real getter for a property read and the real setter for a property write, while a `static init` field assignment must use that field as the dependency graph root without treating a closure-contained write as definite assignment.
- root cause: the dependency collector followed only named static/global functions, treated assignment targets as ordinary reads, and owned the complete `static init` body with one aggregate graph node. It therefore missed `c -> test.get -> c` and `b = value -> foo.set -> b`, while callable substitutions, fake overrides, property access mode, and the field-level owner order were not represented.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 reports `sema_global_var_used_before_initialization` on the `c` read in `test.get` and the `b` read in `foo.set` for `InitializationCheck/static_variable_use_before_init_07.cj`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/GlobalVarChecker.cpp:74-83` maps property reads/writes to getter/setter targets; `307-349` changes the `DefNode` to the assigned static field and collects only the RHS; `418-490` recursively collects callable dependencies; and `554-570` compares use and owner visit order. `InitializationChecker.cpp:787-793` keeps this global dependency diagnostic out of ordinary non-constructor member checking. The marker-free `tmp/cfir-probes/static_initializer_local_lambda_invocation_probe.cj` additionally proves that lambda reads report `sema_used_before_initialization` regardless of read/write invocation order, while writes inside a lambda do not initialize the static field in the enclosing `static init` flow.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/cfa/FirPropertyInitializationAnalyzer.kt`, `analysis/cfa/util/PropertyInitializationInfoCollector.kt`, and `VariableInitializationCheckProcessor.kt`; Kotlin supplies the shared property/accessor and CFG ownership structure, while the graph order and getter/setter semantics come from the official Cangjie implementation.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`.
- repair principle: build initialization edges from the real callable behind each resolved access, select getter versus setter from access mode, and assign each directly initialized static field its own graph order while leaving definite assignment to the existing control-flow state.

## Nested local generic bounds and static-owner parameter identity

- problem type: local generic functions declared inside generic static initializers, fields, lambdas, and property accessors must resolve static members through their own upper bounds, while static-generic dependency checking must distinguish the outer owner's type parameters from shadowing local parameters and concrete use-site substitutions.
- root cause: BODY_RESOLVE called the declaration transformer on function type parameters, whose fallback only advanced the phase and left local `where T <: From<Int64, T>` bounds as unresolved user type refs. After call resolution was restored, the static-generic dependency traversal still compared type parameters by `Name` and treated call-site substitution overrides as declarations owned by their generic class, so a local `T` shadowing the owner `R` and a concrete `GenericStatic<Base>` call were falsely diagnosed.
- official Cangjie evidence: cjc 1.0.5 compiles `generics/generic_static_field_prop/generic_static_nested_func.cj` with zero errors. Probe `tmp/cfir-probes/static_generic_nested_callable_owner_probe.cj` reports exactly two `sema_static_variable_use_generic_parameter` diagnostics for outer owner `T` references inside a lambda and a nested local function, and reports none for the local function's own bounded `U` or the explicitly instantiated `GenericStatic<Base>.make()` call. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/LegalityOfUsage/LegalityOfUsage.cpp:91-150` traverses nested expressions and compares referenced generic declarations against the static declaration's generic owner.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/body/resolve/FirDeclarationsResolveTransformer.kt:112-116,994-1012`; Kotlin resolves each function type parameter's children through the BODY_RESOLVE dispatcher before preparing the local function signature.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirDeclarationsResolveTransformer.kt`; `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirGeneralSemanticsChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: resolve real local type-parameter headers before constructing callable scopes, and represent static-owner dependencies by declaration symbols so lexical shadowing and explicit call-site substitution retain their semantic identities.

- problem type: test-harness directive placement. Four multi-file fixtures placed `// DIAGNOSTICS: -warnings` after a `// FILE:` marker, which is unrepresentable for a Global directive; the harness correctly rejected it. The failure was a fixture-format violation, not a CFIR semantic defect.
- official Cangjie evidence: not applicable. ## OPEN DISCREPANCY (not a fix): `T <: T` self-bound is not diagnosed by cjc 1.0.5

Flagged while gathering evidence for the extend upper-bound recursion problem type. Recorded here so it is not re-derived, and so the contradiction is visible before anyone trusts the earlier entry.

- The earlier entry "Generic upper-bound direct recursion and first invalid-bound reporting" states that graph cycles including direct self-reference `T <: T` must report `GENERIC_PARAM_DIRECTLY_RECURSIVE`.
- Re-probing with `cjc` 1.0.5 (`C:\Users\lin17\.cangjie\sdks\cangjie-1.0.5\bin\cjc.exe`) contradicts that for the *self*-bound case specifically: `func g<T>() where T <: T {}` and `class C<T> where T <: T {}` both compile cleanly, exit 0, zero diagnostics.
- Mechanism: `ExposeGenericUpperBounds` (`external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/PreCheck.cpp:1100`) contains `(void)exposedUpperBounds.erase(genericTy); // Erase itself to avoid invalid looping.` and runs *before* `AssumptionSanityCheck` / `ValidRecursiveConstraintCheck` inside `CheckAssumption` (`PreCheck.cpp:1133`). The self-bound is deleted from the bound set, so no generic upper bound survives for the recursion check to flag.
- Cycles of length >= 2 are still diagnosed, consistent with the earlier entry: `func h<K, U>() where K <: U, U <: K {}` reports `sema_generic_param_directly_recursive`. So only the self-bound sub-case is contradicted, not the whole entry.
- Not acted on: this is a distinct problem type from the recursion/termination fix, and changing it was out of scope for that repair. It needs its own evidence pass to determine whether CFIR currently over-reports on `T <: T`, and whether the earlier conclusion came from a different `cjc` version.

## Extend supertype computation re-enters upper-bound subtype checking (StackOverflowError)

- problem type: computing a type's direct supertypes evaluates constrained `extend` declarations, whose `where` clause requires a subtype decision, which requires supertypes again. With an F-bounded parameter the cycle never terminated and the LLT run died with `StackOverflowError` on both the light-tree and PSI paths.
- root cause: `CfirTypeAwareSupertypeProviderImpl.getDirectSupertypes` was read-cache -> compute -> write-cache with no "computing" marker, so a re-entrant query always missed the cache and recomputed. The cycle ran `getDirectSupertypes` -> `collectEffectiveExtendSupertypes` -> `instantiateExtendSupertypes` -> `createExtendDeclarationSubstitution` -> `matchExtendTargetType` -> `satisfiesUpperBound` -> `AbstractTypeChecker.isSubtypeOf` -> `ConeTypeContext.fastCorrespondingSupertypes` -> `getDirectSupertypes`. The existing `TypeCheckerState` guards (`supertypesDeque`/`supertypesSet`, `argumentsDepth`) could not stop it because `AbstractTypeChecker.isSubtypeOf(context, sub, super)` allocates a fresh state per call, and `collectAllSupertypesWithGivenTypeConstructor` consults `fastCorrespondingSupertypes` before `anySupertype`, bypassing the deque. The `visited` set in `collectEffectiveExtendSupertypes` is per-call and cannot span an `isSubtypeOf` boundary.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 accepts `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/Extend/upperbound_recursive.cj` verbatim with exit 0 and zero diagnostics, so the correct behavior is to terminate silently rather than report a recursion diagnostic. F-bounded `T <: A<T>` is legal because `ValidRecursiveConstraintCheck` (`external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/PreCheck.cpp:954`) gates on bound shape: rule A needs `upper->IsGeneric()`, rule B needs `!upper->IsClassLike()`, and `A<T>` is a class-like constructor application, so neither fires. Extend `where` constraints gate supertype contribution eagerly in `TypeManager::GetAllExtendInterfaceTyHelper` (`external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeManager.cpp:1280`), which skips any extend whose `CheckGenericDeclInstantiation` fails. Termination comes from `TypeManager::IsSubtype` (`TypeManager.cpp:992`), which pre-seeds its `subtypeCache` with `false` before computing and overwrites it with the real answer, under the compiler's own comment that the cache is not for speedup but to avoid recursive judgement on the same types. That is least-fixed-point semantics: assume not-a-subtype on re-entry. The key is the 4-tuple `(leaf, root, implicitBoxed, allowOptionBox)` (`include/cangjie/Sema/TypeManager.h:468-497`). There is no depth cap and no fixed-point iteration on this path.
- additional probes run by the main agent to settle the cache-key question, all with `cjc --error-count-limit all` and the shared preamble `class A<X>`, `interface I`, `class B <: I`, `extend<V> A<V> <: I where V <: I`, `func g<T>() where T <: I`: `g<A<B>>()` exit 0, `g<A<A<B>>>()` exit 0, `g<A<A<A<A<B>>>>>()` exit 0, and `g<A<NotI>>()` exit 1 reporting `'Class-A<Class-NotI>' is not a subtype of 'Interface-I'`. Nested-but-distinct instantiations are therefore separate memo entries that officially answer true, so keying the guard on the type constructor alone would be wrong.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirSupertypesResolution.kt` (`SupertypeComputationStatus` NotComputed/Computing/Computed, with `startComputingSupertypes` writing `Computing` before computing, so the guard is an in-progress marker rather than a completed-visited set), `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/FirCorrespondingSupertypesCache.kt` (keyed on `ConeClassLikeLookupTag`, computed on the default type then projected by pure substitution, with no resolution inside the supplier), and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/ConeTypeContext.kt` plus `SupertypeUtils.kt` (the supertype supplier is read-only and phase-ordered). CFIR's own Kotlin-isomorphic `SupertypeComputationSession` in `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/transformers/CfirSupertypesResolution.kt` covers only SUPER_TYPES-phase declared supertypes, not the lazy extend path. The in-progress idiom follows the existing `expandingAliases` stack guard in `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/TypeExpansionUtils.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/services/CfirTypeAwareSupertypeProviderImpl.kt` only. Added a thread-confined `computingSupertypes` in-progress set, a two-level `isSupertypeComputationReentry` predicate, and moved `fullyExpandedType` up into `getDirectSupertypes` so the in-progress marker and the computation consume the same semantic type, meaning an alias spelling cannot bypass the guard.
- repair principle: the guard sits on `getDirectSupertypes`, the single aggregation point through which roughly 13 call sites obtain supertypes and on which both ends of the cycle land, so it holds for re-entry arriving through any entry point rather than only the extend arc that a per-call-site guard would cover.
- termination argument: level 1 catches an exactly structurally equal re-entry, which is the fixture's shape. Level 2 catches an expansive re-entry, where the type constructor matches and the new query contains an in-progress type as a proper subterm; it is required because level 1 alone can never fire on a chain that grows every round, which is the only shape that makes the in-progress key space unbounded. Level 2 does not move the fixed point, because the larger query can only succeed by returning one level down to decide the contained in-progress type, and that step hits level 1 and yields "does not contribute". Instances sharing a constructor that are smaller or non-containing are still computed normally, which is exactly what the `A<A<B>>` probes require. On re-entry the provisional empty list is returned without being cached, so it cannot poison the completed-result cache; only the real answer is stored, mirroring the official seed-then-overwrite.
- fixtures covered: `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated.testUpperboundRecursive` and `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated.testUpperboundRecursive`.
- fixture correction: none. `upperbound_recursive.cj` is already correct, since `cjc` reports nothing for it.
- documented divergence: the expansive level-2 case has no observed official counterpart, because no probe could construct one that `cjc` itself terminates on. It is a deliberate, documented termination rule for an IDE frontend that must not hang, not a claim of official parity. No fixture in the repository exercises it.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated' --tests '*llt.array.ArrayGenerated' --tests '*VarrayGenerated' --console=plain`
- verification outcome: `testUpperboundRecursive` passes on both paths and `StackOverflowError` no longer appears anywhere in the run (0 occurrences). `llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated` went from 27 failures out of 164 tests to 26 out of 164 on both the light-tree and PSI paths, the single recovered test, with no other test changing state. `llt.varray.VarrayGenerated` held at 3/22 and every `diagnostics*.varray` suite held at 1/2, unchanged from baseline.

## Builtin Array/CPointer constructor calls emitted two conflicting argument-count diagnostics

- problem type: a single call with a trailing lambda and a wrong argument count produced both `TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS` and `WRONG_NUMBER_OF_ARGUMENTS` with partially overlapping, non-nested ranges, so the LLT renderer aborted with `IllegalArgumentException: The outer diagnostic TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS at 110 ends at 128, but the supposedly inner WRONG_NUMBER_OF_ARGUMENTS starting at 122 ends at 137`.
- root cause: two independent components each decided arity. `CfirCallResolver.collectBuiltinArrayConstructorCandidates` pre-attached `TooManyArguments(functionCall, name)` to the synthetic candidate whenever `callInfo.arguments.size > 2`, and `collectBuiltinPointerConstructorCandidates` did the same for `> 1`, both passing the call itself as the offending argument. Because both raw builders deliberately exclude a trailing lambda from the call source, that anchor resolved to `Array<Int64>(1, 2)` at `[110,128)`. Independently `CfirMapArguments.mapCallableArguments` compared 3 arguments against 2 formals and emitted `WrongNumberOfArguments` on `callShape.arityDiagnosticSource`, which `createCallShape` extends through the trailing lambda to `[122,137)`. Both reached `coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic`, which mapped the list unfiltered, producing overlapping siblings that cannot nest.
- official Cangjie evidence: `sema_wrong_number_of_arguments` (`external/cangjie_compiler/include/cangjie/Basic/DiagRefactor/DiagnosticSema.def:28`) is the only general arity diagnostic; "too many" and "too few" are merely different `symptom` strings selected in `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Diags.cpp:45-51`. No general `sema_too_many_arguments` exists, and `sema_cfunc_too_many_arguments` is CFunc-specific and unrelated. Exactly one is emitted per call: all four emission sites return immediately after emitting (`src/Sema/TypeCheckCall.cpp:668`, `:1373`, `:1820`, `:2158`), and overload-candidate diagnostics are stashed by `DiagSuppressor` (`TypeCheckCall.cpp:1989-1990`) with only the winner's replayed (`:2124-2135`). The trailing lambda is folded into the argument list before type checking by `DesugarTrailingClosureExpr` (`src/Sema/Desugar/DesugarBeforeTypeCheck.cpp:441-458`), so only one argument list and one arity comparison ever exist. The official range rule (`Diags.cpp:54-60`) starts at the open parenthesis and ends at the trailing lambda's end when the last argument extends past the close parenthesis. `cjc` 1.0.5 on the fixture reports exactly three diagnostics whose ranges match the fixture's existing inline markers byte-for-byte: `sema_wrong_number_of_arguments` at `[46,57)` covering `() {i => i}`, `sema_undeclared_identifier` at `[91,92)` covering `i`, and `sema_wrong_number_of_arguments` at `[122,137)` covering `(1, 2) {i => i}`. Counter-evidence that the extra diagnostic's anchor is wrong even in isolation: `Array<Int64>(1, 2)` with no trailing lambda produces no arity error officially at all, reporting `sema_cannot_convert_literal` instead, since 2 is the correct arity for `init(size, initElement)` (`external/cangjie_runtime/stdlib/libs/std/core/array.cj:49`).
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/FirArgumentsToParametersMapper.kt`, the sole producer of arity diagnostics, where `TooManyArguments` is constructed only at `:210`, `:253` and `:265`, `NoValueForParameter` at `:312`, and `TooManyArguments.argument` is always a real argument node so nesting is guaranteed by node identity rather than by a check; and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/ResolutionStages.kt:691-703`, the single reporting stage, where the other `mapArguments` callers deliberately discard `mapping.diagnostics`. No Kotlin caller pre-counts `arguments.size` to decide arity, and the mapper computes arity once, after trailing-lambda folding.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/body/CfirCallResolver.kt` only. Both pre-attached `TooManyArguments` sites were removed; `builtinArrayConstructorKinds` now handles the over-arity case by synthesizing the single `INIT_FUNCTION` candidate shape behind a new named `BUILTIN_ARRAY_CONSTRUCTOR_MAX_ARITY` constant, and the pointer path selects its shape from argument count alone, leaving arity judgement entirely to the mapper.
- repair principle: argument count now has exactly one owner, `CfirMapArguments`, which already models the call shape and already enforces one arity diagnostic per mapping via `addWrongNumberOfArguments`, so the competing decision was deleted rather than filtered downstream, which would have left the wrong-owner structure in place.
- note on the surviving `TooManyArguments` site: `CfirMapArguments.kt:116` in `mapVariableAccessArguments` is retained and is legitimate, because it anchors on a real argument expression, matching Kotlin's contract, and lives inside the mapper that owns the decision.
- fixtures covered: `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.array.ArrayGenerated.testArrayInvalidTrailingClosure` and `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.array.ArrayGenerated.testArrayInvalidTrailingClosure`.
- fixture correction: none. `array_invalid_trailing_closure.cj` was verified byte-correct against `cjc`.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '*llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated' --tests '*llt.array.ArrayGenerated' --tests '*VarrayGenerated' --console=plain`
- verification outcome: `testArrayInvalidTrailingClosure` passes on both paths and `IllegalArgumentException` no longer appears in the run (0 occurrences). `llt.array.ArrayGenerated` went from 12 failures out of 30 tests to 11 out of 30 on both paths. Because the same change touches the shared builtin CPointer constructor path, every VArray and CPointer suite was included in the same run as a regression guard: `llt.varray.VarrayGenerated` held at 3/22 on both paths and all seven `diagnostics*` and macro varray suites held at 1/2, unchanged from baseline.

- full-suite regression confirmation (covers both problem types logged above): `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --continue --console=plain` reports `8496 tests completed, 1954 failed, 314 skipped`, against a pre-fix baseline of `1958 failed` on the identical 8497-test surface. A per-suite diff across all 1252 suites shows exactly four changed suites, each -1 and each an improvement: `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated` and `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.Extend.ExtendGenerated` (27 -> 26), `CfirAnalysisLLTTest.llt.array.ArrayGenerated` and `CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTest.llt.array.ArrayGenerated` (12 -> 11). No suite regressed.

## CheckerContext.containingDeclarations symbol migration left 10 consumers filtering on declaration types

- problem type: checker infrastructure regression. `CheckerContext.containingDeclarations` was migrated from `List<CfirDeclaration>` to `List<CfirBasedSymbol<*>>`, but ten consumers still filtered the stack with *declaration* types. Kotlin's `is`/`filterIsInstance` against an unrelated type is compile-clean and simply never matches, so each of these predicates silently evaluated to "nothing found" and the checker built on top of it became dead code. No exception, no warning — the diagnostics just stopped being produced.
- root cause: the migration moved the shared helpers (`findClosest<T : CfirBasedSymbol<*>>`, `findClosestDeclaration<T : CfirDeclaration>` at `cfir/checkers/src/.../context/CheckerContext.kt:417,426`) and several call sites (`CfirExtendSemantics.kt:216`, `CfirCaptureHasShadowVariableChecker.kt:43`, `CfirConstEvalArithmeticChecker.kt:365`, `CfirClosureCaptureUsageChecker.kt:268`, `CfirLambdaExpectedFunctionTypeUtils.kt:83`, `CfirDeclaredUpperBoundContextUtils.kt:140`), but missed every site that inlined its own traversal. The giveaway is that `CfirConstEvalArithmeticChecker.expectedInitializerTypeFor` was migrated while the near-identical `CfirLiteralNumericOverflowChecker.expectedInitializerTypeFor` was not. Two sites additionally compared stack entries by *identity* against a declaration (`dropWhile { it !== function }`, `indexOfLast { it === function }`), which can never match once the stack holds symbols.
- official Cangjie evidence: none needed for the migration itself — it restores already-implemented diagnostics rather than changing any triggering condition, so no semantic claim is made. Official evidence was required only for the one genuine semantic gap the restoration exposed, and is recorded in the following entry.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/context/CheckerContext.kt:38` declares `abstract val containingDeclarations: List<FirBasedSymbol<*>>` — CFIR's refactor mirrors K2 exactly, confirming the seam is right and only the consumers were stale. Kotlin's own consumption is uniformly symbol-typed: `declarationUtils.kt:41,98`, `FirCommonConstructorDelegationIssuesChecker.kt:30` (`lastIsInstanceOrNull<FirRegularClassSymbol>()`), `FirConstructorAllowedChecker.kt:29`, `FirDataObjectContentChecker.kt:29`, `FirConstPropertyChecker.kt:41`.
- CFIR owner files changed (10): `type/CfirUpperBoundViolatedTypeChecker.kt`, `declaration/CfirGeneralSemanticsChecker.kt`, `declaration/CfirMemberBodyDeclarationChecker.kt`, `declaration/CfirConstructorDelegationChecker.kt`, `declaration/CfirFieldVariableThisOrSuperInitializerChecker.kt`, `declaration/CfirTypeParameterBoundsChecker.kt`, `declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`, `expression/CfirConstructorDelegationCallChecker.kt`, `expression/CfirExpressionSemanticsChecker.kt`, `expression/CfirLiteralNumericOverflowChecker.kt`, `expression/CfirMutabilityCheckers.kt`.
- repair principle: the fix is scoped by the *contract* (`containingDeclarations` holds symbols) rather than by the fixtures that surfaced it — every direct consumer in `cfir/checkers/src` was enumerated and migrated, and wherever an already-correct shared helper existed the bespoke traversal was deleted in favour of it (`findClosestDeclaration<T>()`) instead of being rewritten, so the number of places that can drift out of sync again went down rather than up.
- scope check: a full re-scan of all 23 direct `containingDeclarations` consumers in `cfir/checkers/src` reports zero remaining declaration-typed predicates. The three surviving `as? Cfir...` casts (`CfirDeclaredUpperBoundContextUtils.kt:141`, `CfirTypeParameterBoundsChecker.kt:340`, `CfirMutabilityCheckers.kt:250`) all cast *after* projecting through `.cfir`, which is correct.
- fixtures covered: 68 generated suites improved, in 34 perfectly symmetric PSI / light-tree pairs — confirming the fix landed on infrastructure shared by both CFIR entry points rather than on one path. Largest: `llt._class.ClassGenerated` (-13 each path), `llt.function.FunctionGenerated`, `llt.record.RecordGenerated`, `llt.record.mut.MutGenerated` (-7 each), `llt.generics.GenericsGenerated` (-6), `diagnostics2.invalid_declaration.InvalidDeclarationGenerated` and `llt._class.open_modifier.OpenModifierGenerated` (-5), `llt._class.static_call_non_static.StaticCallNonStaticGenerated` (-4), `diagnostics.constructor.ConstructorGenerated` and `llt.generics.generic_constraint_inheritance.GenericConstraintInheritanceGenerated` (-3). No macro suite changed, consistent with the requested non-macro scope.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --continue --console=plain`
- verification outcome: `8496 tests completed, 1612 failed, 314 skipped`, against a pre-fix baseline of `1802 failed` on the identical 8496-test surface — 190 tests recovered. A per-suite diff across all 1252 suites shows 68 improved and zero regressed.

## struct property setters carry mut semantics; getters do not

- problem type: struct mutability context. Exposed by the migration above: once `CfirMutabilityCheckers` actually ran again, `CANNOT_MODIFY_VAR` was wrongly reported for a field assignment inside a `mut prop` setter, breaking 3 previously-passing fixtures on both paths (6 suites, +1 each).
- root cause: `currentImmutableStructMutationContext` decided mut-ness with `outerFunction.status.isMut`. A `CfirPropertyAccessor` resolved status does not inherit `mut` from its owning property — the same non-inheritance the file already documented and worked around for `static` via `isStaticStructMemberContext()`, but with no `mut` counterpart. So every property accessor looked immutable.
- official Cangjie evidence: the rule is accessor-*kind*-based, not property-status-based. `DeclAttributeChecker::CheckStructAttribute` (`external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/DeclAttributeChecker.cpp:210-226`) enables `Attribute::MUT` on the setters of every non-static struct property, and `CheckExtendAttribute` (`:250-257`) does the same for extends whose target `ty->IsStruct()`; getters have it explicitly disabled (`src/AST/Utils.cpp:663`, `src/Sema/TypeChecker.cpp:356`). The consumer, `TypeChecker::TypeCheckerImpl::CheckMutationInStruct` (`src/Sema/TypeCheckAccess.cpp:229-252`), then gates purely on `outFunc->node->TestAnyAttr(Attribute::CONSTRUCTOR, Attribute::MUT)`. `cjc` 1.0.5 probes confirm the distinction, which is invisible if you only read the property's own `mut` keyword: mutating `a` inside a `mut prop` **setter** compiles clean (exit 0, zero diagnostics); inside the same `mut prop` **getter** it fails with `instance member variable 'a' cannot be modified in immutable function`; inside a plain non-`mut` `prop` getter it fails identically. So reading `propertySymbol.status.isMut` — the naive mirror of the `static` workaround — would have been wrong for the getter case.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: none applicable. Accessor mut-ness is a Cangjie value-type rule with no FIR analogue; the structural pattern followed is the file's own existing `isStaticStructMemberContext()`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/expression/CfirMutabilityCheckers.kt` only. Added `isMutStructMemberContext()` beside `isStaticStructMemberContext()`, and routed both mut-context consumers through it.
- repair principle: the "a struct setter carries mut" invariant is encoded once and consumed by both places that ask the question — the mutation check (`currentImmutableStructMutationContext`) and the nested-capture check (`currentStructCaptureContext`) — because official code applies the identical `Attribute::MUT` test in both, `CheckMutationInStruct` and `CanTargetOfRefBeCapturedCaseMutFunc` (`src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr.cpp:166-186`); fixing only the site that failed would have left the capture check reading a different notion of mut-ness.
- fixtures covered: 10 suites improved in 5 PSI / light-tree pairs — `llt._class.class_property.ClassPropertyGenerated`, `llt.property.PropertyGenerated`, `llt.property.import_prop_check.ImportPropCheckGenerated`, `llt.record.RecordGenerated`, `llt.record.property.PropertyGenerated`.
- fixture correction: none. Every fixture involved was already correct; `cjc` was used to confirm the expectation rather than to change it.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --continue --console=plain`
- verification outcome: `1622 failed -> 1612 failed` on the identical 8496-test surface. A per-suite diff across all 1252 suites shows 10 improved and zero regressed; in particular `llt.record.mut.MutGenerated` held at 17 on each path, so the broadened mut context did not cost anything in the family that motivated it.
- residual, explicitly NOT claimed as fixed: `llt.record.mut.MutGenerated` still fails 17 per path. The remaining marker deltas are `INCOMPATIBLE_MUT_MODIFIER_BETWEEN_STRUCT_AND_INTERFACE` (16, owner `CfirInheritanceDeepChecker`), `IMMUTABLE_FUNCTION_CANNOT_ACCESS_MUTABLE_FUNCTION` (12 missing / 4 extra), `CAPTURE_THIS_OR_INSTANCE_FIELD_IN_FUNC` (12), `THIS_AS_EXPRESSION_IN_FUNC` (12, owner `CfirExpressionSemanticsChecker:364`), and an extra `USE_MUTABLE_FUNC_ALONE` (16). These are separate problem types with different owners and need their own evidence passes.

## `static init` is rejected by its own modifier-target classification

- problem type: modifier target checking. `WRONG_MODIFIER_TARGET` was reported on the `static` keyword of every static initializer — 98 spurious occurrences across 74 test methods, with zero corresponding missing occurrences anywhere in the non-macro surface, i.e. pure over-reporting from a single owner. A breakdown of the flagged token/context pairs shows the family is completely homogeneous: 90 `static init` and 8 `static const init`, nothing else.
- root cause: the classification is self-defeating. `actualTargetsFor` (`cfir/checkers/src/.../ModifierCheckerTargets.kt:281-287`) maps a `CfirConstructor` to `ModifierTarget.head(DeclarationKind.STATIC_INITIALIZER)` precisely *when* `declaration.status.isStatic`, but `possibleTargetMap[STATIC_KEYWORD]` was `memberOf(FUNCTION, PROPERTY, VARIABLE)` and did not list `STATIC_INITIALIZER` at any site. So the `static` modifier is what causes the target to be classified `STATIC_INITIALIZER`, and that classification then makes `static` illegal — the modifier can never be accepted. Introduced with the declaration-kind-plus-site modifier model (commit `3df71067f`).
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 accepts `static init()` in a class body (exit 0, zero diagnostics) and in a struct body (exit 0), and also accepts `static const init()` (exit 0), so the fix does not over-legalize the `const` combination that accounts for 8 of the 98. The construct is illegal in `interface` and `extend` bodies, but that is enforced by the **parser**, not by modifier-target checking — `cjc` reports `unexpected constructor in interface body` and `unexpected constructor in extend body`. The modifier-target table therefore does not need to encode a container restriction for this kind, because no unparseable container can ever reach it.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: none needed beyond the model already in place. The `(DeclarationKind, Site)` predicate model and `TargetAllowedPredicate` alignment were established by the existing implementation; this repair does not change the model, only a missing entry in its table.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/ModifierCheckerTargets.kt` only. `STATIC_KEYWORD` becomes `anyOf(memberOf(FUNCTION, PROPERTY, VARIABLE), anySiteOf(STATIC_INITIALIZER))`.
- repair principle: the entry is site-agnostic (`anySiteOf`) because `static` is *constitutive* of the `STATIC_INITIALIZER` target rather than merely permitted on it — no `Site` can make it wrong — which removes the contradiction at its source instead of pinning the table to whichever site `actualTargetsFor` happens to produce today; this also matches the site-agnostic treatment `STATIC_INITIALIZER` already receives elsewhere in the same file (`defaultVisibilityKinds`, and `CONST_KEYWORD`'s `anySiteOf`).
- deliberately not changed: `actualTargetsFor` still classifies both static and non-static constructors with `Site.HEAD`. `Site.HEAD` is documented as "declaration head itself", so a constructor arguably belongs at `Site.MEMBER`; but reclassifying it would also move plain `CONSTRUCTOR`, which visibility modifiers depend on and which is not currently failing. That is a separate problem type and was left alone rather than folded into this repair.
- fixtures covered: 18 suites improved in 9 PSI / light-tree pairs — `llt._class.static_or_global_var.StaticOrGlobalVarGenerated` (-11 each path), `llt.InitializationCheck.InitializationCheckGenerated` (-6), `llt._class.static_init.StaticInitGenerated` (-4), `llt._class.static_or_global_var.static_or_global_var14.StaticOrGlobalVar14Generated`, `llt.const_evaluation.ConstEvaluationGenerated`, `llt.generics.generic_static_field_prop.GenericStaticFieldPropGenerated`, `llt.record.static_init.StaticInitGenerated` (-2 each), `llt.InitializationCheck.static_variable_use_before_init_02.StaticVariableUseBeforeInit02Generated` and `..._06.StaticVariableUseBeforeInit06Generated` (-1 each).
- fixture correction: none. Every fixture involved was already correct; `cjc` was used to confirm the expectation rather than to change it.
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --continue --console=plain`
- verification outcome: `8496 tests completed, 1550 failed, 314 skipped`, against `1612 failed` before this repair on the identical surface — 62 tests recovered. A per-suite diff across all 1252 suites shows 18 improved and zero regressed. A focused pre-check over the affected slice went from 106 failures to 48 with no suite worse.
- residual: the `WRONG_MODIFIER_TARGET` over-reporting family is now fully closed — a re-scan of the whole non-macro surface finds no remaining extra occurrences of this diagnostic. The suites listed above still fail for unrelated reasons (`USED_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION`, const-eval and generic-static problem types), which are separate families.

## Typealias extend supertypes participate in static member scope traversal

- problem type: a class/type qualifier must see static members inherited from an interface introduced by an applicable `extend`, even when the extend target and inherited interface are written through typealiases.
- root cause: `CfirTypeAwareSupertypeProviderImpl` correctly returned the applicable extend parent edge, but `CfirClassUseSiteMemberScope` consumed the returned `ConeTypeAliasType` directly. Parent scope construction attempted symbol lookup with the alias `ClassId`, while containing-name collection stopped at the same alias, so static `pas` and `foos` declared by the expanded `II<C<A>>` interface never entered qualifier lookup. Instance extend members worked because they came from the extend scope rather than the parent-interface scope.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 compiled `tmp/cfir-probes/typealias_extend_transparency_probe.cj` with exit 0 and only two unused-variable warnings; the probe exercises subtype assignment, static property/function access, and instance extend members through `type C<T> = B<T>` and `type I = II<C<A>>`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeManager.cpp` `GetAllExtendInterfaceTyHelper` instantiates each applicable extend interface and feeds it through `GetAllSuperTys`, so lookup receives the real instantiated interface graph rather than stopping at alias spelling.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/SupertypeUtils.kt` (`computePartialExpansion` before each supertype is emitted) and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/FirKotlinScopeProvider.kt` (`lookupSuperTypes(..., substituteTypes = true)` followed by `scopeForSupertype`).
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/providers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/scopes/impl/CfirClassUseSiteMemberScope.kt`.
- repair principle: normalize every direct parent edge at the single member-scope traversal boundary, so declared, extend-derived, type-aware, name-collection, substitution, and provenance paths all consume the same expanded nominal parent type.
- fixtures covered: both PSI and LightTree paths for all 16 fixtures under `cfir/analysis-tests/testData/llt/generics/generic_static_field_prop/`, including the triggering `generic_static_prop06.cj`; guard fixtures `typealias30.cj` and `typealias35.cj` also passed on both paths.
- fixture correction: none for this problem type.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Generics$GenericStaticFieldProp.testGenericStaticProp06' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Generics$GenericStaticFieldProp.testGenericStaticProp06' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias30' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias30' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias35' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias35' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache`.
- focused verification outcome: fresh XML completed all 6 methods with `failures=0 errors=0` for both PSI and LightTree paths.
- family verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Generics$GenericStaticFieldProp' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Generics$GenericStaticFieldProp' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Typealias' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Typealias' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache`.
- family verification outcome: both `GenericStaticFieldProp` suites passed all 17 tests (`34/34`, zero failures). The same run confirmed `typealias30` and `typealias35` remain green; its 22 `Typealias` failures are separate pre-existing/regressed diagnostic, cycle, inference, and call-resolution families and do not include the repaired static-member fixture.

## Operator ambiguity keeps the operator-specific diagnostic classification

- problem type: an overloaded binary operator whose candidates all reject the operand type must report `INVALID_BINARY_OPERATOR`, while ordinary overloaded calls continue to report the shared argument mismatch diagnostic.
- root cause: `ConeAmbiguityError.mapConeAmbiguityError` evaluated `sharedOverloadArgumentTypeMismatchDiagnostic` before the operator-only cascade and classification helpers. Multi-candidate operator failures therefore returned the generic `TYPE_MISMATCH` early and never reached `invalidBinaryOperatorDiagnosticForOperatorAmbiguity`.
- official Cangjie evidence: the existing operator fixtures encode the project diagnostic surface for invalid binary operators; this repair changes only the mapping order after overload resolution and does not alter candidate applicability or Cangjie operator semantics.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: none required for this ordering regression; the existing CFIR operator-specific diagnostic owner and shared-overload owner already represented the two intended classifications.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/diagnostics/coneDiagnosticToCfirDiagnostic.kt`.
- repair principle: classify operator ambiguity at the common `ConeAmbiguityError` mapping boundary before applying the ordinary-call shared mismatch rule, so every operator call shape uses the established operator diagnostic path.
- fixtures covered: `typealias3.cj` and `typealias4.cj` on both PSI and LightTree paths; the `Binary`, `Operator`, and `OperatorOverload` generated slices were also scanned for the same expected-`INVALID_BINARY_OPERATOR`/actual-`TYPE_MISMATCH` regression.
- fixture correction: none.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias3' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias3' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias4' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Typealias.testTypealias4'`.
- focused verification outcome: all four PSI/LightTree methods passed.
- family verification outcome: the expanded `Binary`, `Operator`, and `OperatorOverload` run executed 178 tests; 56 unrelated failures remained, and fresh XML contained no remaining fixture that expected `INVALID_BINARY_OPERATOR` but received only `TYPE_MISMATCH`. The subsequent complete Typealias run also kept `typealias3/4` green on both paths.

## Typealias cycles are broken before expansion

- problem type: direct, generic, and nested typealias reference cycles must report `TYPEALIAS_CYCLE` on every declaration in the cycle without allowing `fullyExpandedType` to recurse indefinitely; independent unused-type-parameter diagnostics must still run on the preserved RHS.
- root cause: CFIR resolved a typealias RHS in a separate path, stored it as `Computed` immediately, and did not recursively visit aliases in the RHS type tree. Its later loop check called `fullyExpandedType` while trying to identify the graph target, so `D = F, F = D` overflowed before the DFS could see either edge. Cycle checkers also identified the error by a reason-string prefix instead of a structured diagnostic kind.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 reports `sema_typealias_cycle` for both declarations in `D -> F -> D` and in `D<T> -> F<Int32> -> D<Rune>`, while also reporting `typealias_unused_type_parameters` for `T` and `U`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/PreCheck.cpp` (`ResolveTypeAlias`, `TypeAliasCircleCheck`, `ConstructDiagInfoForCycle`) resolves all aliases and runs a DFS before replacement; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/Utils.cpp` `GetTypeArgsOfType` traverses the RHS root and nested type components; `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeManager.cpp` stops replacement for declarations marked `IN_REFERENCE_CYCLE`.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/transformers/FirSupertypesResolution.kt` (shared `NotComputed/Computing/Computed` state machine, nested typealias visitation, graph loop breaking, `DiagnosticKind.RecursiveTypealiasExpansion`) and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/TypeExpansionUtils.kt` (expansion relies on the SUPER_TYPES phase to have broken loops first).

## Source-file classifiers outrank imports during non-local lookup

- problem type: a classifier declared by the source-file scope must participate in the ordinary non-local tower group and must not lose to a default-import or package fallback solely because its scope implementation is file-backed.

- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 resolves source declarations before imported declarations in the corresponding multi-file extend-export probes; `external/cangjie_compiler` name lookup classifies source declarations as ordinary non-local declarations rather than package fallback entries.

- repair principle: classify every file-declared top-level symbol at the shared tower-group boundary, so lookup priority is stable for all classifiers and is independent of which file-scope implementation produced the candidate.

## Extend generic bounds use the shared import-reachability model

- problem type: the applicability and export visibility of a generic `extend` must treat a bound type as reachable when it is made visible by either an explicit import or the language's default imports.
- root cause: upper-bound accessibility and inference used separate import scans. One path considered only explicit resolved bindings, another treated absent bindings as globally visible, and the import checker did not collect generic extend bounds. The same bound could therefore be accepted by lookup but rejected by export/accessibility checking.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 accepts the generic extend when its bound is explicitly imported or default-imported and rejects use sites where the bound is not reachable; the official extend lookup checks the instantiated target and its generic constraints under the use-site import environment.

- repair principle: compute explicit/default-import reachability once at the file/import service boundary and make every extend applicability and declaration checker consume that result.

## Primitive synthetic symbols construct primitive semantic types

- problem type: a primitive qualifier such as `Int64` must inherit and resolve static interface members contributed by an applicable `extend` using primitive subtype semantics.
- root cause: the generic `CfirClassLikeSymbol.constructType()` path converted `CfirPrimitiveTypeSymbol` into `ConeClassLikeType(Int64)`. Member and supertype lookup then used the class-like index instead of primitive extend semantics, so `Int64.f<Int16>(1)` could not see the inherited static interface implementation.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 compiles `Extend/extend_lookup/main.cj` with exit code 0 and no diagnostics. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/TypeCheckExpr/NameReferenceExpr.cpp`, `TypeCheckExtend.cpp`, `TypeManager.cpp`, `LookUpImpl.cpp`, and `TypeCheckReference.cpp` show primitive name lookup flowing through extend inheritance; `LookUpImpl.cpp` explicitly permits inherited static members.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/resolve/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/resolve/calls/QualifierReceiver.kt`, `calls/tower/FirTowerResolveTask.kt`, `calls/tower/TowerLevels.kt`, and `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/scopes/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/FirStaticScope.kt`.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/cfir-tree/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/symbols/TypeConstructionUtils.kt`; `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/CfirDeclaredUpperBoundContextUtils.kt`; `cfir/resolve/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/calls/tower/CfirTypeVariableReceiverMemberScopeTowerLevel.kt`; test coverage in `cfir/resolve/test/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/resolve/providers/CfirBuiltinSymbolProviderTest.kt`.
- repair principle: synthetic symbols may provide declaration metadata, but semantic type construction must preserve the classifier kind at the common constructor boundary so every subtype, extend, and member-scope consumer sees `ConePrimitiveType`.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree `Extend/extend_lookup/main.cj`; the provider test asserts primitive symbols construct primitive semantic types.
- fixture correction: none.
- focused verification command: the four-method command selecting PSI and LightTree `ExtendGeneric01.testFailed02` and `ExtendLookup.testMain`.
- focused verification outcome: all four methods passed with fresh XML. The complete PSI and LightTree Extend run retained `ExtendLookup.testMain` green; `:cfir:resolve:test` could not execute the added unit test because existing unrelated unresolved references in `CfirConstraintCompletionTest.kt` stop `compileTestKotlin`, while all main test-task prerequisites containing the changed production files compiled successfully.

## Extend-origin overrides claim the member pair before ordinary visibility diagnostics

- problem type: `CANNOT_WEAKEN_ACCESS_PRIVILEGE` must apply only to a callable that can legally implement or override its inherited parent; a class member that collides with an ancestor type's extend member belongs exclusively to `EXTEND_FUNCTION_CANNOT_OVERRIDDEN`.
- root cause: `CfirInheritanceDeepChecker.checkInheritedMemberKindConsistency` compared visibility before classifying the same callable pair as an extend-origin override. The later extend branch reported the dedicated diagnostic and stopped ordinary cannot-override processing, but it could not retract the already emitted weak-visibility diagnostic.
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 reports only `sema_ambiguous_match` at the call and `sema_extend_function_cannot_overridden` at `C.foo` for `extend_inherit/main_err.cj`; it does not report `sema_weak_visibility`. `external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/StructInheritanceChecker.cpp:1038-1072` classifies and claims extend-member override relations, while `CheckAccessVisibility` at lines 1174-1201 explicitly rejects parents that cannot be implemented; the protected non-open member declared by `extend A` is not an implementable parent.
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/providers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/scopes/impl/AbstractFirUseSiteMemberScope.kt` preserves the direct override graph and base scope; `external/kotlin/compiler/fir/checkers/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/fir/analysis/checkers/declaration/FirOverrideChecker.kt` consumes that classified relation before applying ordinary visibility checks.
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInheritanceDeepChecker.kt`.
- repair principle: classify and claim an extend-origin callable pair after shared return-type comparison but before ordinary visibility and overridability diagnostics, so every pair follows one inheritance relation and one diagnostic-priority path.
- fixtures covered: PSI and LightTree paths for `Extend/extend_export/direct_extend/extend_inherit/main_err.cj`; the complete Extend slices verify that no other extend-origin relation regressed.
- fixture correction: none.
- focused verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Extend$ExtendExport$DirectExtend$ExtendInherit.testMainErr' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Extend$ExtendExport$DirectExtend$ExtendInherit.testMainErr' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --console=plain --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache`.
- focused verification outcome: both selected methods passed (`2/2`) and all production prerequisites compiled.
- family verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$Extend' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$Extend' -x :cfir:analysis-tests:generateTestGeneratorForCfirAnalysisTestsTests --no-daemon --max-workers=1 --quiet --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache`.
- family verification outcome: fresh XML executed 870 Extend tests with 102 failures, down from 104. The corrected per-test marker parser reports `CANNOT_WEAKEN_ACCESS_PRIVILEGE missing=0 extra=0` and retains `EXTEND_MEMBER_CANNOT_SHADOW missing=0 extra=0` across complete PSI and LightTree slices; the remaining failures belong to separately clustered families.

## 子类型 static/非 static 同名成员使用官方的 static_and_non_static 诊断

- problem type: Diagnostics（诊断选择）。子类型成员与继承成员同名但 static 属性不同时，应报 `STATIC_AND_NON_STATIC_MEMBER_CANNOT_HAVE_SAME_NAME`，而非 `INHERIT_MEMBER_KIND_INCONSISTENT`。
- root cause: 测试数据错误。CFIR 的实现本来就与官方一致；8 个 `llt/overload` fixture 把官方 `sema_static_and_non_static_member_cannot_have_same_name` 误标成了 `INHERIT_MEMBER_KIND_INCONSISTENT`，标记范围（子类成员标识符 `foo`）双方一致，只有诊断名不同。
- official Cangjie evidence: `cjc` 1.0.5 `--diagnostic-format=json` 对 8 个 fixture 去标记后逐个编译，全部输出 `"DiagKind": "sema_static_and_non_static_member_cannot_have_same_name"`（例如 `class_extends_class1.cj` 10:5，消息 `static member 'foo' cannot have the same name with non-static member in parent class or interfaces`）。`external/cangjie_compiler/src/Sema/InheritanceChecker/StructInheritanceChecker.cpp:1082-1104` 的 `CheckSameNameInheritanceInfo` 先判断 `child.TestAttr(STATIC) != parentDecl->TestAttr(STATIC)`，命中即报 `sema_static_and_non_static_member_cannot_have_same_name` 并 `return`；`sema_inherit_member_kind_inconsistent` 只在 astKind 不同（1097 行）或 const/非 const 不一致（1412 行）时产生。反向验证：仓库中另外 5 个使用 `INHERIT_MEMBER_KIND_INCONSISTENT` 的 fixture（`class_shadow10/11`、`const_evaluation/err_interface`、`Extend_Refactor/extend_property_conflict_invalid_2/3`）经 `cjc` 确认确实是 `sema_inherit_member_kind_inconsistent`，属于 kind/const 不一致，不在本族内。
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: 无需 —— 本次是 fixture 期望与官方诊断选择不符，CFIR 侧检查器结构未改动。
- CFIR owner files changed: 无（实现无需修改）。
- repair principle: 诊断名归属按官方 `CheckSameNameInheritanceInfo` 的判定顺序划分——static 属性不一致优先于 kind 不一致；据此把整族 fixture 一次性对齐，而不是按单个用例改实现输出。

- fixture correction: 上述 8 个文件的 `<!INHERIT_MEMBER_KIND_INCONSISTENT!>` 改为 `<!STATIC_AND_NON_STATIC_MEMBER_CANNOT_HAVE_SAME_NAME!>`，范围保持在成员标识符不变。

## 继承字段的初始化状态纳入子类构造器跟踪（已修复并验证）

- problem type: Flow Analysis / Diagnostics。子类构造器给父类字段赋值/读取时，`CANNOT_ASSIGN_TO_IMMUTABLE` 与 `USED_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION` 的判定。
- root cause: `analyzeFunctionBody` 的构造器路径调用 `owner.instanceFieldInfos(context)`（`includeInherited` 默认 false），继承字段根本不在跟踪集合内，被分类为 `NOT_TRACKED`，进而一律判为不可写 → 误报 `CANNOT_ASSIGN_TO_IMMUTABLE`。
- official Cangjie evidence（`cjc` 1.0.5）：
  - `let_in_init10-1.cj` 去标记后编译：`sema_cannot_assign_to_immutable` 只出现在 `class D <: E`（父类 `E.b` **有**初始化器）的两处赋值；`class C <: A`（父类 `A.b` **无**初始化器）对 `A.b` 的赋值**不报错**。
  - 探针 `open class A { public let b: Int32; public init() { b = 1 } }` + `class C <: A { init() { super(); this.b = 0 } }` → 报 `sema_cannot_assign_to_immutable`：父字段一旦被其所属类初始化，子类再写入即非法。
  - 探针 `open class A { public let b: Int32 }` + `class C <: A { init() { this.b = 0; this.b = 1 } }` → 只在**第二次**赋值报错：官方在子类构造器内确实跟踪继承字段的初始化状态，首次赋值合法。
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: 无需新增 —— 修复复用本仓库既有能力（`instanceFieldInfos(includeInherited = true)` 的文档已引用官方 `InitializationChecker::GetNonFuncDeclsInSuperClass`）。
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirInitializationCheckers.kt`
  - 构造器路径改用 `instanceFieldInfos(context, includeInherited = true)`；
  - 新增 `inheritedPreInitializedFieldSymbols`，把「已由所属父类完成初始化」的继承字段并入 `preInitializedFields`。
- 「父类是否已初始化自己的字段」的判据（关键）：与同文件 `reportFieldsLeftUninitializedByDefaultConstructor` 保持同一判据——父类只要存在**带函数体的实例构造器**，即视为由它自己负责初始化全部实例字段（此时父类不会报 `CLASS_UNINITIALIZED_FIELD`）；此外带初始化器的字段与主构造成员属性同样计入。父类既无初始化器又无构造器体的字段才是真正未初始化，允许子类构造器首次赋值。
- repair principle: 让继承字段与本类字段走同一套「跟踪集合 + 预初始化集合」机制，并复用仓库既有的「父类是否自行初始化」判据，从而同时修正写入侧（误报不可变）与读取侧（误报未初始化），而不是对某个 fixture 放宽可变性判定。
- fixtures covered: `llt/class/let_in_init/let_in_init10-1.cj`、`let_in_init10-2.cj`、`let_in_init11-1.cj`、`let_in_init12-1.cj`（PSI 与 LightTree 两条路径，共 8 例）。回归对照：`llt/class/class_initialization7.cj`、`llt/Users/UsersTest2/super.cj` 覆盖读取侧。
- 修复过程（两次尝试）：第一版只把「带初始化器 + 主构造成员属性」计入预初始化集合，导致父类在**构造器体内**初始化的字段被当成未初始化，`super.a` / `this.x` 的**读取**被误报 `USED_BEFORE_INITIALIZATION`（`class_initialization7.cj`、`super.cj` 两条路径共 4 例回归）。第二版引入上述「父类有构造器体即自行初始化」判据后回归清零。
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --continue --console=plain`（全量）
- verification outcome: 全量 8415 例，范围内失败由基线 1088 降至 1078；`let_in_init10-1/10-2/11-1/12-1` 两条路径共 8 例转绿，**新增回归 0**。基线取自 `DIFF_CORPUS_2026-08-10.json`。

## 重复父接口诊断锚点：声明级报在声明头，实例化级报在使用点完整类型引用

- problem type: Diagnostics（诊断范围/锚点）。`SUPER_TYPES_DUPLICATE` 在声明级重复时范围过窄（只有名字标识符），在实例化后才显现的重复上 fixture 把锚点错放在声明处。
- root cause:
  - `CfirSupertypesChecker.checkInstantiatedDuplicateSuperInterfaces` 用 `classLikeNameOffsetsDiagnosticSource()` 取范围，只覆盖名字标识符，产出 `interface <!D!>II<!><T>`；testData 中 21 个使用该诊断的文件无一例外把范围写成完整声明头 `<!D!>interface II<T><!>`。
  - `interface_duplicated_02/04/05` 与 `extend_duplicate_interfaces6/10` 的 fixture 锚点/宽度与同族其它 fixture（`interface_duplicated_01`、`_07`）自相矛盾。
- official Cangjie evidence（`cjc` 1.0.5 `--diagnostic-format=json`，取 MainHint Range）:
  - 声明级重复锚在声明起点、宽度 1 列：`interface_duplicated_06` → `10:1-10:2`、`14:1-14:2`、`16:1-16:2`（分别是 `class A<T>`、`class C`、`interface I2` 所在行首）；`interface_duplicated_12` → `6:1-6:2`；`interface_generic3` → `8:1-8:2`；`interface_generic7` → `10:1`、`14:1`、`16:1`、`26:1`、`38:1`、`42:1`。
  - 实例化后才显现的重复锚在**使用点**，不在声明：`interface_duplicated_01` → `9:13-9:14`（`var b = A<Int64>()` 的 `A`）；`interface_duplicated_02` → `9:12-9:13`（`var b: A<Int64>`）；`interface_duplicated_04` → `15:13-15:14`；`extend_duplicate_interfaces6` → `5:9-5:10`（`B<String>()` 的 `B`）。
  - 官方诊断名统一是 `sema_inherit_duplicate_interface`（extend 场景另有 `sema_extend_duplicate_interface`）。
  - 由此得到统一规则：`cjc` 把主位置压成「目标语法元素起点的 1 个字符」；本项目 Diagnostic Range Policy 要求展宽为该元素的完整范围——声明 → 从 `class`/`interface` 关键字到名称与类型参数列表结束；使用点 → 完整类型引用（含类型实参）。
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: 本次是范围策略问题，按 skill 的 Diagnostic Range Policy 直接裁定（policy 自身即证据）；CFIR 侧已有对应实现 `classLikeDeclarationHeaderDiagnosticSource()`，其文档注释即描述「从声明起点到声明名（含类型参数）结束」，无需新建策略。
- CFIR owner files changed: `cfir/checkers/src/org/cangnova/cangjie/cfir/analysis/checkers/declaration/CfirSupertypesChecker.kt`（`checkInstantiatedDuplicateSuperInterfaces` 改用 `classLikeDeclarationHeaderDiagnosticSource()`）。
- repair principle: 声明级重复父接口的诊断源统一走已有的「声明头」source 计算，而不是名字 token；这样同一个 source helper 同时覆盖 PSI 与 LightTree 两条路径上的全部 class/interface/struct/enum 声明，而不是逐 fixture 调整偏移。
- fixtures covered: `interface_duplicated_06.cj`、`interface_duplicated_12.cj`、`interface_generic3.cj`、`interface_generic4.cj`、`interface_generic5.cj`、`interface_generic6.cj`、`interface_generic7.cj`（实现修复）；`interface_duplicated_02.cj`、`interface_duplicated_04.cj`、`interface_duplicated_05.cj`、`extend_duplicate_interfaces6.cj`、`extend_duplicate_interfaces10.cj`（fixture 修正）。均覆盖 PSI 与 LightTree 两条路径。
- fixture correction:
  - `interface_duplicated_02/04/05`：删除声明处 `<!SUPER_TYPES_DUPLICATE!>class A<Q><!>` 标记，改标在 `cjc` 实际报告的使用点 `A<Int64>` / `A<Rune>`。
  - `extend_duplicate_interfaces6/10`：使用点标记由裸标识符 `B` 展宽为完整类型引用 `B<String>` / `B<String, String>`，与同族 `interface_duplicated_01`、`_07` 的写法一致。
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat -I cfir/analysis-tests/build/full-log-init.gradle.kts :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests '...LLTTestGenerated$ExtendsImplementsInterfaceDuplicated' --tests '...LLTPsiTestGenerated$ExtendsImplementsInterfaceDuplicated' --tests '...LLTTestGenerated$Interface$GenericInterfaceInheritance' --tests '...LLTPsiTestGenerated$Interface$GenericInterfaceInheritance' --tests '...LLTTestGenerated$Extend' --tests '...LLTPsiTestGenerated$Extend' --console=plain`
- verification outcome: 938 个用例、106 个失败（全部为该族之外的既有失败）。12 个目标 fixture 的 24 个用例（PSI + LightTree）全部由失败转为通过；与修复前的失败集合逐条比对，**新增失败为 0**。

## 泛型实例化后才显现的重复父接口应报在实例化处，而非声明处

- problem type: Diagnostics（诊断报告位置 + range）。`SUPER_TYPES_DUPLICATE` 在「父接口仅在特定类型实参下才重复」时的归属位置。
- root cause: 测试数据错误。CFIR 实现本来就与官方一致——把该诊断报在**实例化处**并按项目 range policy 展宽为完整类型 token；`interface_duplicated_08.cj` 仍保留旧的**声明处**标记 `<!SUPER_TYPES_DUPLICATE!>class A<Q><!>`，属于同族 02/04/05 已修正后遗漏的最后一个文件。
- official Cangjie evidence（`cjc` 1.0.5 `--diagnostic-format=json`，本会话 `external/cangjie_compiler` 目录为空、不可用，故仅以 cjc 取证）：
  - 探针 p2/p4/p5/p6：`class A<Q> <: I0<Q> & I0<Int64> {}`（以及其 interface 对应形态）在**没有冲突实例化**时**完全不报错**——声明本身合法，`A<String>` 这类非冲突实例化同样不报错。
  - 探针 p1：加上 `var b: A<Int64>` 后报 `sema_inherit_duplicate_interface`，位置在**实例化处** `A`（L6 C12-13），而非声明行。
  - 去标记后的 `interface_duplicated_08.cj` 经 cjc 编译：`Errors=2`，均为 `sema_inherit_duplicate_interface`，分别位于 L25 C12（`var a: A<Int64>`）与 L26 C13（`var b = A<Int64>()`）；第 18 行 `class A<Q>` 声明处**无任何诊断**。文件内 I2/I3/I4/I5 的实例化亦无诊断。
  - 对照探针 p3：`class A <: I0 & I0 {}`（非泛型、字面重复）才报在**声明处**（L3 C1）。两类子情形的归属位置不同，08 属于前一类。
- Kotlin counterpart files consulted: 无需 —— 本次为 fixture 期望与官方诊断位置不符，CFIR 检查器结构未改动。
- CFIR owner files changed: 无（实现无需修改）。
- repair principle: 按官方「重复是否需要类型实参代入才显现」划分归属位置——需代入才显现的报在实例化处、字面重复的报在声明处；据此把整族 fixture 一次性对齐，而不是按单个用例改实现输出。
- fixtures covered: `llt/extends_implements_interface_duplicated/interface_duplicated_02.cj`、`_04.cj`、`_05.cj`（先前已修正）、`_08.cj`（本次补齐），PSI 与 LightTree 两条路径。
- fixture correction: `_08.cj` 删除第 18 行声明处标记，改为在第 25/26 行两处实例化标记 `<!SUPER_TYPES_DUPLICATE!>A<Int64><!>`（range 按项目 policy 展宽至完整 `A<Int64>` token，官方窄锚为首字符 `A`）。
- verification command: `.\gradlew.bat :cfir:analysis-tests:test --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTTestGenerated$ExtendsImplementsInterfaceDuplicated' --tests 'org.cangnova.cangjie.cfir.analysis.tests.CfirAnalysisLLTPsiTestGenerated$ExtendsImplementsInterfaceDuplicated' --console=plain`
